title.en: Volume 88: Treatise on the Western Regions
title.raw: 卷八十八 西域傳 Volume 88: Treatise on the Western Regions

sentences.zh: 註：章節乃維基文庫編輯後加，以方便索引。

sentences.zh: 13 高附國

translations.literal: 13 The State of Gaofu.
translations.idiomatic: Section 13: The kingdom of Gaofu.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，西域內屬，有三十六國。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu, the Western Regions entered dependency and had thirty-six states.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu the Western Regions submitted to Han and comprised thirty-six polities.

sentences.zh: 漢為置使者、校尉領護之。

translations.literal: Han for them appointed envoys and colonels to lead and protect them.
translations.idiomatic: The Han court appointed imperial envoys and colonels to supervise and defend them.

sentences.zh: 宣帝改曰都護，元帝又置戊己二校尉，屯田於車師前王庭。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan changed the title to Protector-General; Emperor Yuan again established the two Gengji colonels and opened military-agricultural colonies at the royal court of Front Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan renamed the office Protector-General of the Western Regions; Emperor Yuan added two Gengji colonels with garrison farms at the seat of the king of Front Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 哀平間，自相分割為五十五國。

translations.literal: Between Emperors Ai and Ping, they divided themselves into fifty-five states.
translations.idiomatic: During the reigns of Emperors Ai and Ping the region splintered into fifty-five states.

sentences.zh: 王莽篡位，貶易侯王，由是西域怨叛，與中國遂絕，並復役屬匈奴。

translations.literal: Wang Mang usurped the throne, degraded and replaced the marquises and kings; therefore the Western Regions resented and rebelled, with China were entirely cut off, and again served under the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Mang seized power and demoted or reshuffled the oasis rulers, the Western Regions turned against Han; ties with the interior were severed, and the oases again fell under Xiongnu control.

sentences.zh: 匈奴斂稅重刻，諸國不堪命，建武中，皆遣使求內屬，願請都護。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu levied taxes heavily and cruelly; the various states could not bear their lot. In the Jianwu era, they all sent envoys requesting to submit internally and asking for a Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu taxed them mercilessly until the kingdoms could endure no more. In the Jianwu period they sent missions one after another asking to enter Han protection and receive a Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 光武以天下初定，未遑外事，竟不許之。

translations.literal: Guangwu, because the realm had only just been pacified, had no leisure for foreign affairs, and in the end did not grant it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Guangwu, with the empire barely settled, had no capacity for the frontier and ultimately refused.

sentences.zh: 會匈奴衰弱，莎車王賢誅滅諸國，賢死之後，遂更相攻伐。

translations.literal: When the Xiongnu grew weak, King Xian of Suoche extirpated and destroyed the various states; after Xian died, they then attacked one another in turn.
translations.idiomatic: As the Xiongnu declined, Xian of Shache (Yarkand) conquered neighboring states; after his death the Tarim dissolved into endless warfare.

sentences.zh: 小宛、精絕、戎廬、且末為鄯善所併。

translations.literal: Xiaoyuan, Jingjue, Ronglu, and Qiemo were annexed by Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyuan, Jingjue, Ronglu, and Qiemo were absorbed by Shanshan (Loulan).

sentences.zh: 渠勒、皮山為於窴所統，悉有其地。

translations.literal: Qule and Pishan were commanded by Yutian; it wholly possessed their territory.
translations.idiomatic: Qule and Pishan fell under Khotan (Yutian), which took their lands in full.

sentences.zh: 郁立、單桓、孤胡、烏貪訾離為車師所滅。

translations.literal: Yuli, Danhuan, Guhu, and Wuzilizi were destroyed by Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: Yuli, Danhuan, Guhu, and Wuzilizi were extinguished by Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 後其國並復立。

translations.literal: Later their states were all re-established.
translations.idiomatic: Later each of these polities was restored.

sentences.zh: 九年，班超遣掾甘英窮臨西海而還。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Ban Chao sent his clerk Gan Ying to reach as far as the Western Sea and return.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year of his western campaign Ban Chao dispatched Gan Ying to explore westward to the Mediterranean before turning back.

sentences.zh: 皆前世所不至，《山經》所未詳，莫不備其風土，傳其珍怪焉。

translations.literal: These were all places previous ages had not reached and the Classic of Mountains and Seas had not detailed in full; none failed to record their customs and soil and transmit their marvels.
translations.idiomatic: Regions no earlier envoy had reached and the Shan hai jing barely mentions—every land had its customs catalogued and its wonders committed to writing.

sentences.zh: 於是遠國蒙奇、兜勒皆來歸服，遣使貢獻。

translations.literal: Thereupon the distant states Mengqi and Doule all came to submit and sent envoys with tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter distant realms such as Mengqi and Doule presented themselves as tributaries and forwarded missions to court.

sentences.zh: 延光二年，敦煌太守張璫上書陳三策，以為「北虜呼衍王常展轉蒲類、秦海之间，專制西域，共為寇鈔。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanguang, the governor of Dunhuang Zhang Dan submitted a memorial presenting three plans, holding that 'the northern barbarians' King Huyan constantly shifts between Barkol and Qinhai, monopolizes control of the Western Regions, and together they raid and plunder.'
translations.idiomatic: In Yanguang 2 (123 CE) Zhang Dan, governor of Dunhuang, laid out three options: the Xiongnu King Huyan was roaming between Barkol and the steppe sea, dominating the Tarim and joining raids on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 今以酒泉屬國吏士二千餘人集昆侖塞，先擊呼衍王，絕其根本，因發鄯善兵五千人脅車師後部，此上計也。

translations.literal: Now use more than two thousand officials and soldiers of the Jiuquan dependent state gathered at Kunlun Pass, first strike King Huyan and cut off his root, then mobilize five thousand Shanshan troops to threaten Rear Cheshi—this is the upper plan.
translations.idiomatic: The best course: mass over two thousand men from the Jiuquan dependent state at Kunlun Pass, strike Huyan first to destroy his base, then bring five thousand Shanshan troops to bear on Rear Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 若不能出兵，可置軍司馬，將士五百人，四郡供其犂牛、穀食，出據柳中，此中計也。

translations.literal: If unable to dispatch troops, one may establish an army major with five hundred officers and soldiers, the four commanderies supplying their plow oxen and grain food, and go out to occupy Liuzhong—this is the middle plan.
translations.idiomatic: If that is impossible, appoint a military official with five hundred men, provisions from the four western commanderies, and hold Liuzhong—the middle option.

sentences.zh: 如又不能，則宜棄交河城，收鄯善等悉使入塞，此下計也。

translations.literal: If again unable, then it is fitting to abandon Jiaohe city, gather Shanshan and the rest and cause them all to enter the passes—this is the lower plan.
translations.idiomatic: Failing that, abandon Jiaohe and withdraw Shanshan and allied states behind the wall—the least desirable plan.

sentences.zh: 」朝廷下其議。

translations.literal: The court submitted his proposal for discussion.
translations.idiomatic: The court circulated Zhang's memorial for debate.

sentences.zh: 尚書陳忠上疏曰：

translations.literal: Minister Chen Zhong submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Supervisor of the Masters of Writing Chen Zhong replied with a memorial:

sentences.zh: 臣聞八蛮之寇，莫甚北虜。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that among the raids of the eight Man tribes, none is graver than the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that of all the frontier threats, none matches the northern nomads.

sentences.zh: 汉兴，高祖窘平城之圍，太宗屈供奉之恥。

translations.literal: When Han arose, the Founding Emperor was embarrassed by the siege of Pingcheng; the Cultivated Emperor bent to the shame of tribute.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of Han, Gaozu was trapped at Pingcheng; Wen Di endured the humiliation of buying peace with gifts.

sentences.zh: 故孝武愤怒，深惟久長之計，命遣虎臣，浮河絕漠，窮破虜庭。

translations.literal: Therefore Emperor Xiaowu was angry and indignant, deeply pondered a long-term plan, ordered and sent fierce ministers, crossed the river and cut across the desert, and utterly broke the barbarian court.
translations.idiomatic: So Emperor Wu, resolved on a lasting strategy, sent his best generals across the Yellow River and deep into the desert until the Xiongnu court itself was shattered.

sentences.zh: 当斯之役，黔首陨于狼望之北，財币縻于盧山之壑，府库单竭，杼柚空虚，算至舟車，赀及六畜。

translations.literal: In this campaign, commoners perished north of Langwang, wealth and coin were exhausted in the ravines of Mount Lu, treasuries were emptied, looms stood idle, levies reached boats and carts, and assessments extended to the six kinds of livestock.
translations.idiomatic: That war cost countless lives beyond the steppe, drained the treasury into mountain gorges, emptied granaries and workshops, and taxed everything from carts and boats down to livestock.

sentences.zh: 夫岂不懷，虑久故也。

translations.literal: How could they not cherish life? They considered what would endure.
translations.idiomatic: It was not bloodlust—it was the knowledge that short-term pain could buy lasting peace.

sentences.zh: 遂开河西四郡，以隔絕南羌，收三十六國，断匈奴右臂。

translations.literal: Thereupon he opened the four commanderies west of the river, in order to isolate the southern Qiang, gathered thirty-six states, and severed the Xiongnu's right arm.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he carved out the four Hexi commanderies to wall off the Qiang, drew thirty-six oasis states into the orbit of Han, and cut off the Xiongnu's western flank.

sentences.zh: 是以单于孤特，鼠窜遠藏。

translations.literal: Therefore the Chanyu stood alone and scattered like rats fleeing far to hide.
translations.idiomatic: The Chanyu was isolated and driven to skulk at the edges of the steppe like a cornered rat.

sentences.zh: 至于宣、元之世，遂備蕃臣，關徼不閉，羽檄不行。

translations.literal: By the eras of Emperors Xuan and Yuan, they finally ranked as outer vassals; passes were not closed and urgent dispatches did not fly.
translations.idiomatic: By the reigns of Xuandi and Yuandi the Xiongnu had become tributary neighbors; frontier gates stayed open and alarm arrows ceased to fly.

sentences.zh: 由此察之，戎狄可以威服，難以化狎。

translations.literal: From this inspect it: Rong and Di can be awed into submission, but are hard to transform through familiarity.
translations.idiomatic: The lesson is plain: steppe peoples yield to strength, not to gentle persuasion.

sentences.zh: 西域内附日久，区区東望扣關者數矣，此其不乐匈奴慕汉之效也。

translations.literal: The Western Regions have long been internally attached; pitifully gazing east and knocking at the passes has occurred repeatedly—this is the effect of their not delighting in the Xiongnu and admiring Han.
translations.idiomatic: The oases have leaned toward Han for generations; time and again they have hammered on the Jade Gate because they dread the Xiongnu and look to the empire for succor.

sentences.zh: 今北虜已破車師，势必南攻鄯善，棄而不救，則諸國从矣。

translations.literal: Now the northern barbarians have already broken Cheshi; the situation must lead them south to attack Shanshan—if abandoned and not rescued, then the various states will follow.
translations.idiomatic: The nomads have smashed Cheshi and will surely drive on Shanshan; if we stand aside, every kingdom along the southern route will follow their lead.

sentences.zh: 若然，則虜財贿益增，胆势益殖，威臨南羌，與之交連。

translations.literal: If it be so, then the barbarians' wealth and bribes will increase more, their daring and power will grow more, their might will press on the southern Qiang, and with them they will join and connect.
translations.idiomatic: They would grow rich on plunder, bolder by the day, and bring the southern Qiang into their orbit.

sentences.zh: 如此，河西四郡危矣。

translations.literal: Like this, the four commanderies west of the river are endangered.
translations.idiomatic: At that point the four Hexi commanderies themselves would be in peril.

sentences.zh: 河西既危，不得不救，則百倍之役兴，不訾之费發矣。

translations.literal: Once the west of the river is endangered, one cannot but rescue it—then labor a hundredfold arises and incalculable expense is unleashed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Hexi is threatened we would have to pour in troops anyway—at vastly greater cost than steady frontier stewardship.

sentences.zh: 議者但念西域絕遠，恤之烦费，不见先世苦心勤劳之意也。

translations.literal: Those who debate only think that the Western Regions are extremely distant and that pitying them is troublesome and costly—they do not see the painstaking labor of intent of former generations.
translations.idiomatic: Critics harp on distance and expense yet ignore why our forebears invested so heavily in the west.

sentences.zh: 方今邊境守御之具不精，内郡武卫之備不修，敦煌孤危，遠來告急。

translations.literal: At present border defense equipment is not refined, inner commandery martial guard preparations are not repaired, Dunhuang stands alone in peril and from afar comes reporting urgent distress.
translations.idiomatic: Our frontier garrisons are ill equipped, interior reserves are thin, and Dunhuang—already isolated—sends desperate pleas from afar.

sentences.zh: 復不辅助。

translations.literal: If again one does not aid them.
translations.idiomatic: If we refuse aid again,

sentences.zh: 内无以慰劳吏民，外无以威示百蛮。

translations.literal: Within there is no means to console officials and people; without there is no means to awe and display to the hundred Man tribes.
translations.idiomatic: we comfort neither our own officials nor the frontier peoples, and we show the border tribes that Han's authority is hollow.

sentences.zh: 蹙國减土，經有明诫。

translations.literal: Shrinking the state and diminishing territory—the classics contain clear warnings.
translations.idiomatic: The classics are plain: yielding territory only invites ruin.

sentences.zh: 臣以為敦煌宜置校尉，案旧增四郡屯兵，以西撫諸國。

translations.literal: Your servant considers that Dunhuang ought to have a colonel established, investigate the old model and increase garrison troops in the four commanderies, to pacify the various states to the west.
translations.idiomatic: I urge that we post a colonel at Dunhuang, reinforce the four western commanderies as in former times, and steady the oases from there.

sentences.zh: 庶足折冲萬里，震怖匈奴。

translations.literal: Perhaps this suffices to repel conflict ten thousand li away and terrify the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: That alone can deter invasion from the horizon and keep the Xiongnu in fear.

sentences.zh: 帝納之，乃以班勇為西域長史，將驰刑士五百人，西屯柳中。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted it; thereupon he appointed Ban Yong Chief Clerk of the Western Regions, led five hundred commuting convict soldiers, and encamped west at Liuzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved: Ban Yong became Chief Clerk of the Western Regions with five hundred penal troops and a base at Liuzhong.

sentences.zh: 勇遂破平車師。

translations.literal: Yong thereupon defeated and pacified Cheshi.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Yong then crushed Cheshi and restored order.

sentences.zh: 自建武至于延光，西域三絕三通。

translations.literal: From Jianwu down to Yanguang, the Western Regions three times were cut off and three times connected.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Jianwu and Yanguang eras Han authority over the Tarim rose and fell three times.

sentences.zh: 顺帝永建二年，勇復擊降焉耆。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongjian of Emperor Shun, Yong again attacked and subdued Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjian 2 (127 CE) of Emperor Shun, Ban Yong forced Yanqi (Karashahr) to surrender.

sentences.zh: 於是龜兹、疏勒、于胘、莎車等十七國皆來服从，而烏孙、葱嶺已西遂絕。

translations.literal: Thereupon Qiuci, Shule, Yugu, Suoche, and seventeen states all came to submit and obey, but Wusun and west of the Pamirs were then cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Kucha, Kashgar, Khotan, Yarkand, and twelve other states renewed their allegiance, though ties with Wusun and everything beyond the Pamirs lapsed.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝以伊吾旧膏腴之地，傍近西域，匈奴资之，以為鈔暴，復令开設屯田，如永元時事，置伊吾司馬一人。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, the emperor, because Yiwu was formerly fertile fat land, close beside the Western Regions, which the Xiongnu supplied and used for raiding and violence, again ordered opening and establishing military colonies, as in the affairs of Yongyuan times, and appointed one Yiwu major.
translations.idiomatic: That same year the court reopened the garrison farms at Yiwu—rich soil that the Xiongnu had used as a staging ground—mirroring the Yongyuan settlement and posting a single Yiwu major.

sentences.zh: 自陽嘉以後，朝威稍损，諸國骄放，轉相陵伐。

translations.literal: From Yangjia onward, court prestige gradually diminished; the various states grew arrogant and unrestrained and turned on one another in bullying attacks.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yangjia era (132–135 CE) imperial prestige faded; oasis kings grew arrogant and preyed on each other.

sentences.zh: 元嘉二年，長史王敬為于窴所沒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuanjia, Chief Clerk Wang Jing was taken by Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 2 (152 CE) Chief Clerk Wang Jing was captured by Khotan.

sentences.zh: 永兴元年，車師後王復反攻屯營。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongxing, the rear king of Cheshi again turned and attacked the encampment.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongxing 1 (153 CE) the king of Rear Cheshi rebelled and struck the Han camp.

sentences.zh: 虽有降首，曾莫惩革，自此浸以疏慢矣。

translations.literal: Although there were those who surrendered their heads, none were truly punished and reformed; from this they gradually became negligent and lax.
translations.idiomatic: Even when rulers pledged submission, nothing changed their behavior, and respect for Han steadily eroded.

sentences.zh: 班固記諸國風土人俗，皆已詳備《前書》。

translations.literal: Ban Gu recorded the customs and peoples of the various states—all are already detailed completely in the Former Book.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Gu's Western Regions account in the Hanshu already covers local customs in full.

sentences.zh: 今撰建武以後其事異于先者，以為《西域傳》，皆安帝末班勇所記云。

translations.literal: Now compiling after Jianwu those affairs that differ from before, making the Treatise on the Western Regions—all are what Ban Yong recorded at the end of Emperor An.
translations.idiomatic: Here we record only what changed after Guangwu's restoration, drawing on Ban Yong's notes from late in Emperor An's reign.

sentences.zh: 西域内屬諸國，東西六千餘里，南北千餘里，東極玉門、陽關，西至葱嶺。

translations.literal: The various states internally dependent of the Western Regions, east-west more than six thousand li, north-south more than one thousand li, east reaching Yumen and Yang Pass, west reaching the Pamirs.
translations.idiomatic: The tributary states of the Western Regions stretch some six thousand li east to west and over a thousand li north to south—from Yumen and Yang Pass in the east to the Pamirs in the west.

sentences.zh: 其東北與匈奴、烏孙相接。

translations.literal: Its northeast connects with the Xiongnu and Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: To the northeast they border the Xiongnu confederation and Wusun.

sentences.zh: 南北有大山，中央有河。

translations.literal: South and north have great mountains; in the center is a river.
translations.idiomatic: Massifs wall the basin north and south; a river runs down the middle.

sentences.zh: 其南山東出金城，與汉南山屬焉。

translations.literal: Its southern mountains east emerge at Jincheng and belong with Han's southern mountains.
translations.idiomatic: The southern range reaches eastward into Jincheng commandery and joins the Qilian chain inside Han territory.

sentences.zh: 其河有两源，一出葱嶺東流，一出于窴南山下北流，與葱嶺河合，東注蒲昌海。

translations.literal: Its river has two sources: one emerges from the Pamirs and flows east; one emerges below Yutian's southern mountains and flows north, joins with the Pamirs river, and pours east into Puchang Sea.
translations.idiomatic: The Tarim draws two headwaters—one eastward off the Pamirs, another north from the Kunlun south of Khotan—that merge and empty east into Lake Lop (Puchang).

sentences.zh: 蒲昌海一名盐泽，去玉門三百餘里。

translations.literal: Puchang Sea is also called Salt Marsh; it is more than three hundred li from Yumen.
translations.idiomatic: Puchang—also called the Salt Marsh—lies a little over three hundred li west of Yumen Pass.

sentences.zh: 自敦煌西出玉門、陽關，涉鄯善，北通伊吾千餘里，自伊吾北通車師前部高昌壁千二百里，自高昌壁北通後部金满城五百里。

translations.literal: From Dunhuang west exiting Yumen and Yang Pass, crossing Shanshan, north connects to Yiwu over one thousand li; from Yiwu north connects to Front Cheshi's Gaochang rampart twelve hundred li; from Gaochang rampart north connects to Rear Department's Jincheng five hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: West from Dunhuang through Yumen and Yang Pass one crosses Shanshan and reaches Yiwu in over a thousand li; another twelve hundred li north from Yiwu lies the Gaochang garrison of Front Cheshi, and five hundred li beyond that lies Jincheng in Rear Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 此其西域之門户也，故戊己校尉更互屯焉。

translations.literal: This is the gateway of the Western Regions; therefore the Gengji colonels rotate garrisoning there.
translations.idiomatic: These passes are the funnel into the Tarim, which is why the Gengji colonels alternate postings there.

sentences.zh: 伊吾地宜五谷、桑麻、蒲萄。

translations.literal: Yiwu's land suits the five grains, mulberry and hemp, and grapes.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwu's soil supports grain, hemp, mulberry, and vineyards.

sentences.zh: 其北又有柳中，皆膏腴之地。

translations.literal: North of it again is Liuzhong—all are fertile fat lands.
translations.idiomatic: Liuzhong to the north is equally rich farmland.

sentences.zh: 故汉常與匈奴争車師、伊吾，以制西域焉。

translations.literal: Therefore Han constantly contended with the Xiongnu over Cheshi and Yiwu, in order to control the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the perennial Han–Xiongnu struggle for Cheshi and Yiwu—whoever holds them commands the western oases.

sentences.zh: 自鄯善逾葱嶺出西諸國，有两道。

translations.literal: From Shanshan crossing the Pamirs exiting to the western various states, there are two routes.
translations.idiomatic: West of Shanshan two roads cross the Pamirs into Transoxiana.

sentences.zh: 傍南山北，陂河西行至莎車，為南道。

translations.literal: Along the south mountains' north, skirting the river west proceeding to Suoche, this is the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: The southern road hugs the northern foot of the Kunlun, follows the river west to Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 南道西逾葱嶺，則出大月氏、安息之國也。

translations.literal: The southern route west crossing the Pamirs then exits to the states of Greater Yuezhi and Parthia.
translations.idiomatic: West of the Pamirs it opens onto Greater Yuezhi and Parthia.

sentences.zh: 自車師前王庭随北山，陂河西行至疏勒，為北道。

translations.literal: From Front Cheshi royal court following the north mountains, skirting the river west proceeding to Shule, this is the northern route.
translations.idiomatic: The northern road leaves the king of Front Cheshi, tracks the southern slope of the Tianshan, and runs west to Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 北道西逾葱嶺，出大宛、康居、奄蔡焉。

translations.literal: The northern route west crossing the Pamirs exits to Dayuan, Kangju, and Yancai.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the Pamirs it reaches Ferghana, Kangju, and the Alans.

sentences.zh: 出玉門，經鄯善、且末、精絕三千餘里至拘彌。

translations.literal: Exiting Yumen, passing Shanshan, Qiemo, and Jingjue, over three thousand li to Jumi.
translations.idiomatic: From Yumen Pass through Shanshan, Qiemo, and Jingjue is more than three thousand li to Jumi.

sentences.zh: 拘彌國

translations.literal: The State of Jumi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Jumi.

sentences.zh: 拘彌國，居寧彌城，去長史所居柳中四千九百里，去洛陽萬二千八百里。

translations.literal: The State of Jumi dwells at Ningmi city; from the Chief Clerk's residence Liuzhong it is four thousand nine hundred li; from Luoyang it is twelve thousand eight hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Jumi had its capital at Ningmi—four thousand nine hundred li from the chief clerk's seat at Liuzhong and twelve thousand eight hundred li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 領户二千一百七十三，口七千二百五十一，胜兵千七百六十人。

translations.literal: It leads households two thousand one hundred seventy-three, mouths seven thousand two hundred fifty-one, victorious soldiers one thousand seven hundred sixty persons.
translations.idiomatic: It counted 2,173 households, 7,251 people, and 1,760 men under arms.

sentences.zh: 顺帝永建四年，于窴王放前杀拘彌王兴，自立其子為拘彌王，而遣使者貢獻于汉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongjian of Emperor Shun, King Fangqian of Yutian killed King Xing of Jumi, established his own son as king of Jumi, and sent envoys to offer tribute to Han.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjian 4 (129 CE) Fangqian of Khotan murdered Jumi's king Xing, installed his own son on the throne, and still sent tribute missions to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 敦煌太守除由上求讨之，帝赦于窴罪，令歸拘彌國，放前不肯。

translations.literal: The governor of Dunhuang Chu You submitted upward requesting to punish them; the emperor pardoned Yutian's crime, ordered return of Jumi state, Fangqian refused.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Chu You of Dunhuang asked permission to attack; the court forgave Khotan on condition it restore Jumi, but Fangqian refused.

sentences.zh: 陽嘉元年，徐由遣疏勒王臣槃發二萬人擊于窴，破之，斩首數百级，放兵大掠，更立兴宗人成國為拘彌王而還。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yangjia, Xu You sent King Chenpan of Shule to mobilize twenty thousand men to strike Yutian, defeated them, beheaded several hundred ranks, released troops to plunder greatly, again established Xing's clansman Chengguo as king of Jumi and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In Yangjia 1 (132 CE) Xu You had Kashgar's king Chenpan march twenty thousand men against Khotan, routed it, took hundreds of heads, let his troops sack the countryside, enthroned Xing's kinsman Chengguo in Jumi, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 至灵帝熹平四年，于窴王安國攻拘彌，大破之，杀其王，死者甚眾。

translations.literal: By the fourth year of Xiping of Emperor Ling, King Anguo of Yutian attacked Jumi, greatly broke them, killed their king, and the dead were very many.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiping 4 (175 CE) Anguo of Khotan stormed Jumi, slew its king, and left great slaughter.

sentences.zh: 戊己校尉、西域長史各發兵辅立拘彌侍子定兴為王。

translations.literal: The Gengji colonel and Chief Clerk of the Western Regions each dispatched troops to assist in establishing Jumi's hostage son Dingxing as king.
translations.idiomatic: The Gengji colonel and the chief clerk sent troops to install Dingxing—the hostage prince at court—as king of Jumi.

sentences.zh: 時人眾裁有千口。

translations.literal: At that time people altogether had only a thousand mouths.
translations.idiomatic: The realm now numbered barely a thousand souls.

sentences.zh: 其國西接于窴三百九十里。

translations.literal: Its state west connects to Yutian three hundred ninety li.
translations.idiomatic: Its western frontier lay three hundred ninety li from Khotan.

sentences.zh: 于窴國

translations.literal: The State of Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Yutian (Khotan).

sentences.zh: 于窴國，居西城，去長史所居五千三百里，去洛陽萬一千七百里。

translations.literal: The State of Yutian dwells at Xicheng; from the Chief Clerk's residence five thousand three hundred li; from Luoyang eleven thousand seven hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan's capital was Xicheng—5,300 li from the chief clerk's headquarters and 11,700 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 領户三萬二千，口八萬三千，胜兵三萬餘人。

translations.literal: It leads households thirty-two thousand, mouths eighty-three thousand, victorious soldiers over thirty thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: It mustered 32,000 households, 83,000 people, and more than 30,000 soldiers.

sentences.zh: 建武末，莎車王贤强盛，攻并于窴，徙其王俞林為骊歸王。

translations.literal: At the end of Jianwu, King Xian of Suoche was strong and flourishing, attacked and annexed Yutian, and moved its king Yulin to be king of Ligui.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Jianwu era Xian of Yarkand conquered Khotan and demoted King Yulin to the petty throne of Ligui.

sentences.zh: 明帝永平中，于窴將休莫霸反莎車，自立為于窴王。

translations.literal: In the Yongping era of Emperor Ming, Yutian's general Xiumoba rebelled against Suoche and established himself as king of Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Ming's Yongping reign Khotan's general Xiumoba threw off Yarkand and crowned himself king.

sentences.zh: 休莫霸死，兄子广德立，後遂灭莎車，其國轉盛。

translations.literal: Xiumoba died; his elder brother's son Guangde was established; afterward they extinguished Suoche, and its state turned flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiumoba died, his nephew Guangde took over, destroyed Yarkand, and built Khotan into the dominant power.

sentences.zh: 从精絕西北至疏勒十三國皆服从。

translations.literal: From Jingjue northwest to Shule thirteen states all submitted and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: From Jingjue northwest to Kashgar thirteen kingdoms acknowledged his authority.

sentences.zh: 而鄯善王亦始强盛。

translations.literal: And the king of Shanshan also for the first time became strong and flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Shanshan's king grew strong at the same time.

sentences.zh: 自是南道目葱嶺以東，唯此二國為大。

translations.literal: From this on the southern route from east of the Pamirs, only these two states were great.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Pamirs along the southern silk road only these two realms mattered.

sentences.zh: 自于窴經皮山，至西夜、子合、德若焉。

translations.literal: From Yutian passing Pishan, arriving at Xiye, Zihe, and Deruo.
translations.idiomatic: From Khotan the route runs through Pishan to Xiye, Zihe, and Deruo.

sentences.zh: 西夜國

translations.literal: The State of Xiye.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Xiye.

sentences.zh: 西夜國，一名漂沙，去洛陽萬四千四百里。

translations.literal: The State of Xiye, one name is Piaosha; from Luoyang fourteen thousand four hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Xiye—also called Piaosha—lay 14,400 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 户二千五百，口萬餘，胜兵三千人。

translations.literal: Households two thousand five hundred, mouths over ten thousand, victorious soldiers three thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: It had 2,500 households, upward of 10,000 residents, and 3,000 troops.

sentences.zh: 地生白草，有毒，國人煎以為药，傅箭镞，所中即死。

translations.literal: The land grows white grass, which is poisonous; the state's people decoct it to make medicine, smear arrowheads, and those struck immediately die.
translations.idiomatic: A toxic white grass grows there; locals boil it into a poison for arrowheads—a scratch means death.

sentences.zh: 《汉書》中误云西夜、子合是一國，今各自有王。

translations.literal: In the Han Shu mistakenly says Xiye and Zihe were one state; now each has its own king.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanshu wrongly merged Xiye with Zihe; in fact each has its own ruler.

sentences.zh: 子合國

translations.literal: The State of Zihe.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Zihe.

sentences.zh: 子合國，居呼鞬谷。

translations.literal: The State of Zihe dwells at Hujiangu valley.
translations.idiomatic: Zihe occupied the Hujian valley.

sentences.zh: 去疏勒千里。

translations.literal: It is one thousand li from Shule.
translations.idiomatic: It lies a thousand li from Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 領户三百五十，口四千，胜兵千人。

translations.literal: It leads three hundred fifty households, four thousand mouths, one thousand victorious soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: It had 350 households, 4,000 people, and 1,000 troops fit for service.

sentences.zh: 德若國

translations.literal: The State of Deruo.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Deruo.

sentences.zh: 德若國，領户百餘，口六百七十，胜兵三百五十人。

translations.literal: The State of Deruo leads over one hundred households, six hundred seventy mouths, three hundred fifty victorious soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Deruo counted just over 100 households, 670 inhabitants, and 350 soldiers under arms.

sentences.zh: 東去長史居三千五百三十里，去洛陽萬二千一百五十里，與子合相接。

translations.literal: East from the Chief Clerk's residence three thousand five hundred thirty li; from Luoyang twelve thousand one hundred fifty li; it connects with Zihe.
translations.idiomatic: It was 3,530 li east of the chief clerk's headquarters, 12,150 li from Luoyang, and bordered Zihe.

sentences.zh: 其俗皆同。

translations.literal: Their customs are all the same.
translations.idiomatic: Their ways of life were identical.

sentences.zh: 烏弋山离國

translations.literal: The State of Wuyi Shanli.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Wuyi Shanli (Alexandria in Arachosia).

sentences.zh: 自皮山西南經烏秅，涉悬度，历罽宾，六十餘日行至烏弋山离國，地方數千里，時改名排持。

translations.literal: From Pishan southwest passing Wuna, crossing Hanging Pass, passing through Jibin, over sixty days' travel reaches the State of Wuyi Shanli; its territory is several thousand li; at times renamed Paichi.
translations.idiomatic: From Pishan one travels southwest through Wuna, crosses the perilous Hanging Pass, skirts Kashmir, and after more than sixty days reaches Wuyi Shanli—a realm thousands of li across, occasionally recorded under the alternate name Paichi.

sentences.zh: 復西南馬行百餘日至條支。

translations.literal: Again southwest by horse over one hundred days to Tiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Another hundred days' ride southwest brings one to Tiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 條支國

translations.literal: The State of Tiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Tiaozhi.

sentences.zh: 條支國城在山上，周回四十餘里。

translations.literal: The city of the State of Tiaozhi is on a mountain; its circumference is over forty li.
translations.idiomatic: Tiaozhi's capital stood on a mountain ringed by more than forty li of walls.

sentences.zh: 臨西海，海水曲环其南及東北，三面路絕，唯西北隅通陆道。

translations.literal: It borders the Western Sea; sea water bends and encircles its south and northeast; three sides have roads cut off; only the northwest corner connects with land routes.
translations.idiomatic: It fronts the western ocean; the sea wraps around the south and northeast so that three sides are inaccessible by land, leaving only a northwest passage.

sentences.zh: 土地暑湿，出師子、犀牛、封牛、孔雀、大雀。

translations.literal: The land is hot and damp; it produces lions, rhinoceroses, hill oxen, peacocks, and great birds.
translations.idiomatic: The climate is torrid and humid; the region yields lions, rhinos, zebu, peacocks, and giant ostriches.

sentences.zh: 大雀其卵如甕。

translations.literal: The great birds' eggs are like jars.
translations.idiomatic: The ostriches lay eggs as large as wine jars.

sentences.zh: 轉北而東，復馬行六十餘日至安息。

translations.literal: Turning north then east, again by horse over sixty days to Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: Bear north and eastward another sixty days on horseback and one reaches Parthia.

sentences.zh: 後役屬條支，為置大將，臨領諸小城焉。

translations.literal: Later it served under Tiaozhi; for it was appointed a great general who oversaw the various small cities.
translations.idiomatic: Later it fell under Tiaozhi's sway; a senior commander was installed to administer its towns.

sentences.zh: 安息國

translations.literal: The State of Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Parthia (Anxi).

sentences.zh: 安息國，居和椟城，去洛陽二萬五千里。

translations.literal: The State of Anxi dwells at Heducheng; from Luoyang twenty-five thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Parthia had its seat at Heducheng, 25,000 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 北與康居接，南與烏弋山离接。

translations.literal: North it connects with Kangju; south it connects with Wuyi Shanli.
translations.idiomatic: It bordered Kangju on the north and Wuyi Shanli on the south.

sentences.zh: 地方數千里，小城數百，户口胜兵最為殷盛。

translations.literal: Its territory is several thousand li; several hundred small cities; households and victorious soldiers are the most flourishing abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Its territory ran thousands of li across hundreds of walled towns; population and military manpower were among the richest of the western lands.

sentences.zh: 其東界木鹿城，号為小安息，去洛陽二萬里。

translations.literal: Its eastern border is Mulu city, titled Lesser Anxi; from Luoyang twenty thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Its eastern march ended at Mulu, known as Lesser Parthia—20,000 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 自安息西行三千四百里至阿蛮國。

translations.literal: From Anxi west traveling three thousand four hundred li reaches the State of Aman.
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand four hundred li west of Parthia lies Aman.

sentences.zh: 从阿蛮西行三千六百里至斯宾國。

translations.literal: From Aman west traveling three thousand six hundred li reaches the State of Sibin.
translations.idiomatic: Another 3,600 li west from Aman brings one to Sibin.

sentences.zh: 从斯宾南行度河，又西南至于罗國九百六十里，安息西界極矣。

translations.literal: From Sibin south proceeding crossing the river, again southwest to the State of Yuluo nine hundred sixty li—Anxi's western border ends.
translations.idiomatic: South from Sibin one crosses a river, then southwest 960 li to Yuluo—Parthia's farthest western frontier.

sentences.zh: 自此南乘海，乃通大秦。

translations.literal: From here south riding the sea, then connects to Daqin.
translations.idiomatic: Southward by sea from that point one reaches Daqin.

sentences.zh: 其土多海西珍奇異物焉。

translations.literal: Its lands have many western-sea rare strange things.
translations.idiomatic: Those shores yield many curiosities from beyond the western ocean.

sentences.zh: 大秦國

translations.literal: The State of Daqin.
translations.idiomatic: The realm of Daqin (the Roman East).

sentences.zh: 大秦國，一名犁鞬，以在海西，亦云海西國。

translations.literal: The State of Daqin, one name is Lijian; because it is west of the sea, also called the Western Sea State.
translations.idiomatic: Daqin—also called Lijian—lies beyond the western sea and is therefore styled the Western Sea realm.

sentences.zh: 地方數千里，有四百餘城。

translations.literal: Its territory is several thousand li; it has over four hundred cities.
translations.idiomatic: Its domains stretch thousands of li and encompass more than four hundred cities.

sentences.zh: 小國役屬者數十。

translations.literal: Small states serving under it are several tens.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen lesser realms pay it tribute.

sentences.zh: 以石為城郭。

translations.literal: They use stone for walls and outer walls.
translations.idiomatic: Their city walls are built of stone.

sentences.zh: 列置邮亭，皆垩塈之。

translations.literal: They array and establish post stations; all are whitewashed.
translations.idiomatic: Postal relays line the roads, each station whitewashed.

sentences.zh: 有松柏諸木百草。

translations.literal: There are pine, cypress, various trees, and hundred grasses.
translations.idiomatic: Pines, cypresses, and many other trees and herbs grow there.

sentences.zh: 人俗力田作，多种树蚕桑。

translations.literal: People's customs vigorously farm fields, mostly plant trees and mulberry for silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: The people farm intensively and cultivate orchards and mulberry for silk.

sentences.zh: 皆髡头而衣文绣，乘輜軿白盖小車，出入擊鼓，建旌旗幡帜。

translations.literal: All shave their heads and wear patterned embroidery; they ride covered carriages with white canopies; going out and entering they strike drums and raise banners, pennants, and flags.
translations.idiomatic: They shave their heads, wear brocade, ride light carriages under white parasols, announce coming and going with drums, and travel behind colored banners.

sentences.zh: 所居城邑，周圜百餘里。

translations.literal: The cities they dwell in surround over one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Their chief cities sprawl across well over a hundred li.

sentences.zh: 城中有五宫，相去各十里。

translations.literal: Inside the city there are five palaces; each separated by ten li.
translations.idiomatic: The capital contains five palaces spaced ten li apart.

sentences.zh: 宫室皆以水精為柱，食器亦然。

translations.literal: Palace chambers all use crystal for pillars; eating vessels are likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Crystal columns adorn the halls, and even tableware is cut from the same stone.

sentences.zh: 其王日游一宫，听事五日而後遍。

translations.literal: Its king each day tours one palace; hearing affairs, in five days then he has completed the round.
translations.idiomatic: The king spends each night in a different palace and completes the circuit every fifth day.

sentences.zh: 常使一人持囊随王車，人有言事者，即以書投囊中，王室宫發省，理其枉直。

translations.literal: Constantly they dispatch one person holding a bag following the king's carriage; when people have matters to speak, they immediately cast writings into the bag; when the royal palace opens and examines, it decides their wrong and right.
translations.idiomatic: An attendant walks beside the royal carriage with a leather sack; petitioners drop written appeals inside, and later the palace clerks empty the bag and judge each case on its merits.

sentences.zh: 各有官曹文書。

translations.literal: Each has official bureaus and documents.
translations.idiomatic: Every bureau keeps its own archives.

sentences.zh: 置三十六將，皆会議國事。

translations.literal: They establish thirty-six generals; all convene and deliberate state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty-six commanders meet in council to settle national policy.

sentences.zh: 其王无有常人。

translations.literal: Their king does not have a constant person.
translations.idiomatic: The throne does not pass by hereditary right alone.

sentences.zh: 皆简立贤者。

translations.literal: All select and establish worthy persons.
translations.idiomatic: The worthiest candidate is chosen to rule.

sentences.zh: 國中灾異及風雨不時，辄废而更立，受放者甘黜不怨。

translations.literal: When in the state disasters and prodigies occur and wind and rain are untimely, then they dismiss and replace; those who receive dismissal willingly accept demotion without resentment.
translations.idiomatic: If calamity strikes or the rains fail, the ruler is deposed for another; the fallen sovereign accepts blame without complaint.

sentences.zh: 其人民皆長大平正，有類中國，故谓之大秦。

translations.literal: Its people are all tall and even upright, resembling China; therefore it is called Great Qin.
translations.idiomatic: The populace is tall and fair like the Chinese themselves—hence the name Daqin, “Great Qin.”

sentences.zh: 土多金银奇宝，有夜光璧、明月珠、骇鸡犀、珊瑚、虎魄、琉璃、琅玕、硃丹、青碧。

translations.literal: The land has much gold, silver, and strange treasures: night-shining disks, bright-moon pearls, rhino horn that startles chickens, coral, amber, colored glass, langgan, cinnabar red, green jasper.
translations.idiomatic: The soil yields gold, silver, and rarities—phosphorescent jade, luminous pearls, patterned rhino horn, coral, amber, glass, langgan beads, cinnabar, and blue-green gems.

sentences.zh: 刺金缕绣，织成金缕罽、杂色绫。

translations.literal: Embroidered gold-thread needlework, woven gold-thread felts, multicolored damasks.
translations.idiomatic: Artisans stitch gold-thread embroidery and weave brocades, gold-shot felts, and polychrome silks.

sentences.zh: 作黄金涂、火浣市。

translations.literal: They make gold coating and fire-washing cloth.
translations.idiomatic: They gild ware in gold and weave asbestos cloth that survives flame.

sentences.zh: 又有细布，或言水羊毳，野蚕茧所作也。

translations.literal: Again there is fine cloth; some say water-sheep down, made from wild silkworm cocoons.
translations.idiomatic: Their finest linen—said to be carded from “sea sheep” or spun from wild silkworm cocoons—is prized abroad.

sentences.zh: 合会諸香，煎其汁以為蘇合。

translations.literal: They combine various fragrances and decoct their juice to make storax balsam.
translations.idiomatic: Perfumers blend resins into storax oil.

sentences.zh: 凡外國諸珍異皆出焉。

translations.literal: In general all foreign various precious strange things come forth there.
translations.idiomatic: Every exotic treasure known to the western trade originates there.

sentences.zh: 以金银為钱，银钱十当金钱一。

translations.literal: They use gold and silver for coin; ten silver coins equal one gold coin.
translations.idiomatic: Gold and silver circulate as coinage at a ratio of one gold piece to ten silver.

sentences.zh: 與安息、天竺交市于海中，利有十倍。

translations.literal: With Anxi and Tianzhu they exchange market on the sea; profit has tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: Maritime trade with Parthia and India returns tenfold profit.

sentences.zh: 其人質直，市无二价。

translations.literal: Its people are honest and straight; the market has no two prices.
translations.idiomatic: Merchants are scrupulous; goods have a single fair price.

sentences.zh: 谷食常贱，國用富饶。

translations.literal: Grain food is always cheap; state resources are rich and abundant.
translations.idiomatic: Grain stays cheap and the treasury overflows.

sentences.zh: 邻國使到其界首者，乘驿詣王都，至則给以金钱。

translations.literal: When neighboring states' envoys arrive at its border head, they ride post stations to the royal capital; when they arrive then they are supplied gold coin.
translations.idiomatic: Foreign envoys who reach the frontier are rushed by relay to the capital and presented with gold on arrival.

sentences.zh: 其王常欲通使于汉，而安息欲以汉缯彩與之交市，故遮阂不得自达。

translations.literal: Its king constantly wished to communicate envoys with Han, but Anxi wished to use Han's silks and brocades to exchange market with them; therefore blocked and obstructed, they could not reach themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Roman rulers longed to open direct ties with Han, but Parthia monopolized the silk trade and blocked every embassy.

sentences.zh: 至桓帝延熹九年，大秦王安敦遣使自日南徼外獻象牙、犀角、玳瑁，始乃一通焉。

translations.literal: By Emperor Huan's Yanxi ninth year, the king of Daqin Andun dispatched envoys from beyond the frontier of Rinan to offer ivory, rhino horn, and tortoiseshell—only then was there one communication.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Yanxi 9 of Emperor Huan (166 CE), when King Antoninus sent envoys from beyond Rinan with ivory, rhinoceros horn, and hawksbill shell, did an embassy finally reach Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 其所表貢，并无珍異，疑傳者过焉。

translations.literal: What they displayed as tribute had no precious strangeness; suspected that transmitters exaggerated.
translations.idiomatic: The gifts were hardly worthy of Rome—later readers suspected the story had grown in the telling.

sentences.zh: 或云其國西有弱水、流沙，近西王母所居处，几于日所入也。

translations.literal: Some say west of its state there are Weak Water and Flowing Sands, near the dwelling place of the Queen Mother of the West, almost where the sun enters.
translations.idiomatic: Some place Daqin west of the Weak River and shifting sands, near the mythic haunts of Xiwangmu at the sunset's edge.

sentences.zh: 《汉書》云「从條支西行二百餘日，近日所入」，則與今書異矣。

translations.literal: The Han Shu says, “From Tiaozhi west traveling over two hundred days, near where the sun enters”—then it differs from present texts.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanshu claims two hundred days west of Tiaozhi brings one to the sunset—which does not match later itineraries.

sentences.zh: 前世汉使皆自烏弋以還，莫有至條支者也。

translations.literal: In former generations Han envoys all returned from Wuyi onward; none reached Tiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Han missions turned back east of Wuyi; none had seen Tiaozhi itself.

sentences.zh: 又云「从安息陆道绕海北行出海西至大秦，人庶連屬，十里一亭，三十里一置，终无盗贼寇警。

translations.literal: Again it says, “From Anxi by land route circling the sea north proceeding out to sea west to Daqin, people and multitude connect continuously; ten li one pavilion, thirty li one station; in the end no robbers or bandit alarms.”
translations.idiomatic: The same text describes a coast road from Parthia to Daqin lined with people, a relay post every ten li, a larger station every thirty, and perfect safety from bandits.

sentences.zh: 而道多猛虎、師子，遮害行旅，不百餘人赍兵器，辄為所食」。

translations.literal: But the road has many fierce tigers and lions; they intercept and harm travelers; if not over one hundred persons carrying weapons, then they are eaten by them.”
translations.idiomatic: Yet tigers and lions wait along the road, and any party with fewer than a hundred armed men is devoured.

sentences.zh: 又言「有飞桥數百里可度海北諸國」。

translations.literal: Again it says, “There are flying bridges several hundred li that can cross to the various states north of the sea.”
translations.idiomatic: It also speaks of hundred-li bridges spanning the sea to the northern kingdoms.

sentences.zh: 所生奇異玉石諸物，谲怪多不經，故不記云。

translations.literal: The strange jade and stone things produced there are deceitful and bizarre, mostly not orthodox; therefore not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Such marvels read like fantasy and are omitted here.

sentences.zh: 大月氏國

translations.literal: The State of Greater Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of the Greater Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 大月氏國，居蓝氏城，西接安息，四十九日行，東去長史所居六千五百三十七里，去洛陽萬六千三百七十里。

translations.literal: The State of Greater Yuezhi dwells at Lanshi city; west connects to Anxi, forty-nine days' travel; east from the Chief Clerk's residence six thousand five hundred thirty-seven li; from Luoyang sixteen thousand three hundred seventy li.
translations.idiomatic: The Kushan court sat at Lanshi—forty-nine days west of Parthia, 6,537 li east of the chief clerk's headquarters, and 16,370 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 户十萬，口四十萬，胜兵十餘萬人。

translations.literal: Households one hundred thousand, mouths four hundred thousand, victorious soldiers over one hundred thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: It registered 100,000 households, 400,000 people, and more than 100,000 soldiers under arms.

sentences.zh: 初，月氏為匈奴所滅，遂遷於大夏，分其國為休密、雙靡、貴霜、駙頓、都密，凡五部翕侯。

translations.literal: At first, the Yuezhi were destroyed by the Xiongnu, thereupon moved to Bactria, and divided their state into Xiumi, Shuangmi, Guishuang, Fudun, and Dumi—altogether five divisions of yabghus.
translations.idiomatic: Driven from the steppe by the Xiongnu, the Yuezhi resettled in Bactria and split into five tribal confederations: Xiumi, Shuangmi, Guishuang, Fudun, and Dumi.

sentences.zh: 後百餘歲，貴霜翕侯丘就卻攻滅四翕侯，自立為王，國號貴霜。

translations.literal: After over one hundred years, the Guishuang yabghu Qiujiuque attacked and extinguished the four yabghus, established himself as king, and the state's title was Guishuang.
translations.idiomatic: A century later Qiujiuque of Guishuang crushed the other four chiefs, proclaimed himself king, and took Guishuang as his dynastic name.

sentences.zh: 侵安息，取高附地。

translations.literal: He invaded Anxi and took Gaofu territory.
translations.idiomatic: He invaded Parthia and seized the Gaofu region.

sentences.zh: 又滅濮達、罽賓，悉有其國。

translations.literal: Again he destroyed Puda and Jibin and wholly possessed their states.
translations.idiomatic: He overran Puda and Kashmir and annexed both realms.

sentences.zh: 丘就卻年八十餘死，子閻膏珍代為王。

translations.literal: Qiujiuque at age over eighty died; his son Yangaozhen succeeded as king.
translations.idiomatic: Qiujiuque died in his eighties; his son Yangaozhen ascended the throne.

sentences.zh: 復滅天竺，置將一人監領之。

translations.literal: Again he destroyed Tianzhu and appointed one general to supervise and lead it.
translations.idiomatic: He conquered northern India and stationed a resident general to govern it.

sentences.zh: 月氏自此之後，最為富盛，諸國稱之，皆曰貴霜王。

translations.literal: From this after, the Yuezhi were the richest and most flourishing; the various states called them, all saying King of Guishuang.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuezhi empire henceforth towered over the region; neighbors spoke only of the King of Guishuang.

sentences.zh: 漢本其故號，言大月氏云。

translations.literal: Han based on their old title, speaks of Greater Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Chinese documents still use their ancient name and call them the Greater Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 高附國

translations.literal: The State of Gaofu.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Gaofu.

sentences.zh: 高附國，在大月氏西南，亦大國也。

translations.literal: The State of Gaofu is southwest of Greater Yuezhi; it is also a great state.
translations.idiomatic: Gaofu lay southwest of the Yuezhi heartland and ranked as a major power.

sentences.zh: 其俗似天竺，而弱，易服。

translations.literal: Its customs resemble Tianzhu, but it is weak and easy to subdue.
translations.idiomatic: Its culture resembles India's, yet the realm is weak and quick to submit.

sentences.zh: 善贾贩，内富于財。

translations.literal: They are good at trading and peddling; internally rich in wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Its merchants thrive and the kingdom is wealthy.

sentences.zh: 所屬无常，天竺、罽宾、安息三國强則得之，弱則失之，而未尝屬月氏。

translations.literal: What it belongs to is not constant; when the three states Tianzhu, Jibin, and Anxi are strong then they obtain it, when weak then they lose it, but it has never belonged to the Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: It changed hands with whichever of India, Kashmir, or Parthia held the upper hand; it had never been a stable dependency of the Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 《汉書》以為五翕侯數，非其实也。

translations.literal: The Han Shu considered it one of the five yabghu count—not its actuality.
translations.idiomatic: The Hanshu wrongly listed Gaofu among the five yabghus.

sentences.zh: 後屬安息。

translations.literal: Later it belonged to Anxi.
translations.idiomatic: It later fell under Parthia.

sentences.zh: 及月氏破安息，始得高附。

translations.literal: When the Yuezhi broke Parthia, only then did they obtain Gaofu.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the Yuezhi shattered Parthia did they secure Gaofu.

sentences.zh: 天竺國

translations.literal: The State of Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: The realm of Tianzhu (India).

sentences.zh: 天竺國，一名身毒，在月氏之東南數千里。

translations.literal: The State of Tianzhu, one name is Shendu; it is several thousand li southeast of the Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: India—also called Shendu—lies several thousand li southeast of the Yuezhi domains.

sentences.zh: 俗與月氏同，而卑湿暑热。

translations.literal: Customs are the same as the Yuezhi, but low-lying, damp, hot summer.
translations.idiomatic: Customs mirror the northwestern Indians', but the climate is low, humid, and sweltering.

sentences.zh: 其國臨大水。

translations.literal: Its state borders a great water.
translations.idiomatic: The country fronts a great river.

sentences.zh: 乘象而战。

translations.literal: They ride elephants to fight.
translations.idiomatic: They fight from elephant howdahs.

sentences.zh: 其人弱于月氏，修浮图道，不杀伐，遂以成俗。

translations.literal: Its people are weaker than the Yuezhi; they cultivate the Buddha way, do not kill or attack, thereupon it becomes custom.
translations.idiomatic: They are less warlike than the Yuezhi; Buddhism forbids killing, and that ethic has shaped daily life.

sentences.zh: 从月氏、高附國以西，南至西海，東至磐起國，皆身毒之地。

translations.literal: From Yuezhi and Gaofu state westward, south reaching the Western Sea, east reaching Panqi state—all are Shendu lands.
translations.idiomatic: From the Yuezhi and Gaofu frontiers westward, south to the ocean and east to Panqi, lies the Indian cultural sphere.

sentences.zh: 身毒有别城數百，城置長。

translations.literal: Shendu has several hundred separate cities; each city establishes an elder.
translations.idiomatic: India contains hundreds of walled towns, each overseen by a magistrate.

sentences.zh: 别國數十，國置王。

translations.literal: Separate states are several tens; each state establishes a king.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen kingdoms each enthrones its own ruler.

sentences.zh: 虽各小異，而俱以身毒為名，其時皆屬月氏。

translations.literal: Although each differs slightly, yet all take Shendu as name; at that time all belonged to the Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Local titles vary, yet foreigners bundle them under “Shendu”; in this era they all answered to the Yuezhi.

sentences.zh: 月氏杀其王而置將，令统其人。

translations.literal: The Yuezhi killed their kings and appointed generals, ordering them to rule their people.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuezhi executed native kings and installed military governors.

sentences.zh: 土出象、犀、玳瑁、金、银、铜、铁、铅、锡，西與大秦通，有大秦珍物。

translations.literal: The soil produces elephants, rhinoceroses, tortoiseshell, gold, silver, copper, iron, lead, tin; west it connects with Daqin and has Daqin precious things.
translations.idiomatic: The land yields ivory, rhino horn, hawksbill, and every metal; Roman luxuries arrive via the western trade.

sentences.zh: 又有细布、好毾氍、諸香、石蜜、胡椒、姜、黑盐。

translations.literal: Again there is fine cloth, good tapestries, various fragrances, rock honey, pepper, ginger, black salt.
translations.idiomatic: Exports include fine cotton, carpets, aromatics, cane sugar, pepper, ginger, and black salt.

sentences.zh: 和帝時，數遣使貢獻，後西域反畔，乃絕。

translations.literal: In Emperor He's time, repeatedly they dispatched envoys with tribute; afterward the Western Regions rebelled and turned away, then it was cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor He missions arrived often; after the Western Regions revolted, contact ceased.

sentences.zh: 至桓帝延熹二年、四年，頻从日南徼外來獻。

translations.literal: By Emperor Huan's Yanxi second and fourth years, repeatedly they came from beyond Rinan's frontier to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Huan, missions from beyond Rinan arrived again in Yanxi 2 and Yanxi 4 with tribute.

sentences.zh: 世傳明帝梦见金人，長大，顶有光明，以问群臣。

translations.literal: Tradition transmits that Emperor Ming dreamed of a golden man, tall and large, with brightness atop his head; he asked his various ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Legend says Emperor Ming dreamed of a towering golden figure crowned with light and polled his ministers.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「西方有神，名曰佛，其形長丈六尺而黄金色。

translations.literal: Someone said: “In the west there is a spirit, named Buddha; its form is one zhang six chi in height and golden in color.”
translations.idiomatic: A courtier answered that in the west stood a god called Buddha—sixteen chi tall and the color of gold.

sentences.zh: 」帝於是遣使天竺，问佛道法，遂于中國图画形象焉。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the emperor dispatched envoys to Tianzhu, inquired about the Buddha way and dharma, and then in China painted and depicted images.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent envoys to India to inquire into the Buddha's teaching and soon welcomed icons painted within China itself.

sentences.zh: 楚王英始信其术，中國因此颇有奉其道者。

translations.literal: Prince Ying of Chu first believed in its art; therefore within China there were quite a few who practiced its way.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying of Chu was the first notable convert; thereafter Buddhists began to appear in the interior.

sentences.zh: 後桓帝好神，數祀浮图、老子，百姓稍有奉者，後遂轉盛。

translations.literal: Later Emperor Huan favored spirits, repeatedly sacrificing to stupas and Laozi; commoners gradually had some who practiced; afterward it turned increasingly flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Huan honored both Buddhist stupas and Laozi; popular devotion grew and Buddhism flourished.

sentences.zh: 東离國

translations.literal: The State of Dongli.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Dongli.

sentences.zh: 東离國，居沙奇城，在天竺東南三千餘里，大國也。

translations.literal: The State of Dongli dwells at Shaqi city; it is over three thousand li southeast of Tianzhu; it is a great state.
translations.idiomatic: Dongli had its capital at Shaqi, more than three thousand li southeast of India—a substantial realm.

sentences.zh: 其土气、物類與天竺同。

translations.literal: Its soil and climate and creature kinds are the same as Tianzhu.
translations.idiomatic: Climate and productions matched those of India.

sentences.zh: 列城數十，皆称王。

translations.literal: Arrayed cities are several tens; all style themselves kings.
translations.idiomatic: Dozens of walled towns each styled its lord a king.

sentences.zh: 大月氏伐之，遂臣服焉。

translations.literal: Greater Yuezhi attacked them; thereupon they submitted and served.
translations.idiomatic: The Kushans invaded and brought Dongli to heel.

sentences.zh: 男女皆長八尺，而怯弱。

translations.literal: Men and women are all eight chi tall, yet timid and weak.
translations.idiomatic: The people stood eight chi tall but were timid in battle.

sentences.zh: 乘象、骆驼，往來邻國。

translations.literal: They ride elephants and camels, coming and going among neighboring states.
translations.idiomatic: They traveled among neighbors on elephants and camels.

sentences.zh: 有寇，乘象以战。

translations.literal: When there are raiders, they ride elephants to fight.
translations.idiomatic: When attacked, they fought from elephants.

sentences.zh: 栗戈國

translations.literal: The State of Lige.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Lige.

sentences.zh: 栗戈國，屬康居。

translations.literal: The State of Lige belongs to Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Lige was a dependency of Kangju.

sentences.zh: 出名馬、牛、羊、蒲萄眾果，其土水美，故蒲萄酒特有名焉。

translations.literal: It produces famous horses, cattle, sheep, grapes and many fruits; its soil and water are fine; therefore grape wine is especially renowned.
translations.idiomatic: It exported horses, livestock, grapes, and orchard fruit; the wine was celebrated.

sentences.zh: 严國，在奄蔡北，屬康居，出鼠皮以输之。

translations.literal: The State of Yan is north of Yancai, belongs to Kangju, and produces marten skins to convey as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Yan lay north of Alania under Kangju and paid tribute in furs.

sentences.zh: 奄蔡國

translations.literal: The State of Yancai.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Yancai (Alania).

sentences.zh: 奄蔡國，改名阿兰聊國，居地城，屬康居。

translations.literal: The State of Yancai changed its name to the State of Alanliao; it dwells at Dicheng; it belongs to Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Yancai—renamed Alanliao—with its seat at Dicheng remained subject to Kangju.

sentences.zh: 土气温和，多桢松、白草。

translations.literal: Soil and climate are mild; many zhen pines and white grasses.
translations.idiomatic: The climate was temperate and pine and white grass grew thick.

sentences.zh: 民俗衣服與康居同。

translations.literal: Popular customs and clothing are the same as Kangju.
translations.idiomatic: Dress and custom matched Kangju.

sentences.zh: 莎車國

translations.literal: The State of Suoche.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Shache (Yarkand).

sentences.zh: 莎車國，西經蒲犁、无雷至大月氏，東去洛陽萬九百五十里。

translations.literal: The State of Suoche, west passes Puli and Wulei to Greater Yuezhi; east from Luoyang ten thousand nine hundred fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: Westward the road ran through Puli and Wulei to the Yuezhi lands; the capital lay 10,950 li east of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 匈奴单于因王莽之乱，略有西域，唯莎車王延最强，不肯附屬。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu Chanyu on account of Wang Mang's turmoil briefly possessed the Western Regions; only King Yan of Suoche was strongest and refused to attach and serve.
translations.idiomatic: While the Xiongnu exploited Wang Mang's chaos to seize the Tarim, King Yan of Yarkand alone remained powerful and independent.

sentences.zh: 元帝時，尝為侍子，長于京師，慕乐中國，亦復参其典法。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yuan's time, he once was a hostage prince, grew up in the capital, admired and delighted in China, and also participated in its statutes and laws.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuandi he had served as a hostage and grew up at court, absorbing Han ritual and law.

sentences.zh: 常敕諸子，当世奉汉家，不可负也。

translations.literal: He constantly instructed his sons that they ought generation after generation to serve the Han house and must not betray it.
translations.idiomatic: He charged his heirs never to betray the Han house.

sentences.zh: 天凤五年，延死，谥忠武王，子康代立。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Tianfeng, Yan died, posthumous title King Zhongwu; his son Kang succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: Yan died in Tianfeng 5 and received the posthumous title King Zhongwu; his son Kang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 光武初，康率傍國拒匈奴，拥卫故都護吏士妻子千餘口，檄書河西，问中國动静，自陳思慕汉家。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangwu, Kang led neighboring states to resist the Xiongnu, embraced and guarded over one thousand persons of wives and children of former Protector-General officials and soldiers, sent proclamations to Hexi, inquired about China's movements, and himself declared longing for the Han house.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Guangwu's reign Kang rallied neighboring states against the Xiongnu, sheltered more than a thousand dependents of the old western garrison, sent word into Hexi asking after the interior, and pledged loyalty to Han.

sentences.zh: 建武五年，河西大將軍竇融乃承制立康為汉莎車建功懷德王、西域大都尉，五十五國皆屬焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Jianwu, Grand General of Hexi Dou Rong then received mandate and established Kang as Han Suoche King Who Establishes Merit and Cherishes Virtue, Grand Colonel of the Western Regions; fifty-five states all belonged to him.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 5 Dou Rong invested Kang as king of Han's Shache with the titles “Merit” and “Cherishing Virtue,” named him Grand Colonel of the Western Regions, and fifty-five states acknowledged him.

sentences.zh: 九年，康死，谥宣成王。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, Kang died, posthumous title King Xucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Kang died in the ninth year and was posthumously named King Xucheng.

sentences.zh: 弟贤代立，攻破拘彌、西夜國，皆杀其王，而立其兄康两子為拘彌、西夜王。

translations.literal: Younger brother Xian succeeded, attacked and broke Jumi and the State of Xiye, killed their kings in both cases, and established two sons of his elder brother Kang as kings of Jumi and Xiye.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Xian took the throne, overran Jumi and Xiye, executed both kings, and enthroned two of Kang's sons on those thrones.

sentences.zh: 十四年，贤與鄯善王安并遣使詣阙貢獻，於是西域始通。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year, Xian and King An of Shanshan together dispatched envoys to the palace to offer tribute; thereupon the Western Regions first connected.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year Xian and the king of Shanshan jointly sent tribute missions to Luoyang and the Tarim corridor reopened.

sentences.zh: 葱嶺以東諸國皆屬贤。

translations.literal: East of the Pamirs the various states all belonged to Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Every kingdom east of the Pamirs acknowledged Xian.

sentences.zh: 十七年，贤復遣使奉獻，請都護。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Xian again dispatched envoys presenting tribute, requesting a Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he sent another embassy begging for a Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 天子以问大司空竇融，以為贤父子兄弟相约事汉，款诚又至，宜加号位以镇安之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven asked Minister of Works Dou Rong; he held that Xian's father and sons and brothers had agreed generation after generation to serve Han, sincerity had again arrived—it was fitting to add titles and ranks to pacify and stabilize them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor consulted Dou Rong, who argued that Xian's family had long honored Han in good faith and deserved investiture to stabilize the west.

sentences.zh: 帝乃因其使，赐贤西域都護印绶，及車旗黄金锦绣。

translations.literal: The emperor then through his envoy bestowed on Xian the Protector-General of the Western Regions seal-cord, as well as chariot banners of gold thread brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Through the envoy the emperor awarded Xian the seal of Protector-General with chariot banners and gold brocade.

sentences.zh: 敦煌太守裴遵上言：「夷狄不可假以大权，又令諸國失望。

translations.literal: Governor of Dunhuang Pei Zun submitted upward saying: “Yi and Di cannot be lent great authority; moreover it causes the various states to lose hope.”
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zun of Dunhuang protested that barbarians must not wield such power and that the oasis kings would despair.

sentences.zh: 」詔書收還都護印绶，更赐贤以汉大將軍印绶。

translations.literal: ” An edict ordered retrieval of the Protector-General seal-cord and again bestowed on Xian the Han Grand General seal-cord.
translations.idiomatic: An edict recalled the Protector-General insignia and substituted the seal of Han Grand General.

sentences.zh: 其使不肯易，遵迫夺之，贤由是始恨。

translations.literal: His envoy refused to exchange; Zun forced and seized it; Xian from this began to resent.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy refused the swap, Pei Zun seized the seal by force—Xian's resentment began there.

sentences.zh: 而犹诈称大都護，移書諸國，諸國悉服屬焉，号贤為单于。

translations.literal: Yet he still falsely styled himself Grand Protector-General, sent letters to the various states; the various states all submitted and belonged to him; they titled Xian Chanyu.
translations.idiomatic: Xian still styled himself Protector-General in letters to the oases, won their obedience, and accepted the title Chanyu.

sentences.zh: 贤浸以骄横，重求赋税，數攻龜兹諸國，諸國愁惧。

translations.literal: Xian gradually became arrogant and domineering, repeatedly demanded taxes, repeatedly attacked Qiuci and various states; the various states worried and feared.
translations.idiomatic: He grew arrogant, doubled levies, and repeatedly struck Kucha and its neighbors until they lived in dread.

sentences.zh: 二十一年冬，車師前王、鄯善、焉耆等十八國俱遣子入侍，獻其珍宝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year winter, Front Cheshi king, Shanshan, Yanqi, and eighteen states together sent sons to attend court and presented their precious treasures.
translations.idiomatic: That winter eighteen realms including Front Cheshi, Shanshan, and Yanqi sent hostage princes and treasure to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 及得见，皆流涕稽首，愿得都護。

translations.literal: When they obtained audience, all wept tears and knocked heads, wishing to obtain a Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: At audience they wept and kowtowed, pleading for a Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 天子以中國初定，北邊未服，皆還其侍子，厚赏赐之。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven, because China had only just been pacified and the northern border was not yet subdued, returned all their attendant sons and richly rewarded them.
translations.idiomatic: The court, with the interior still unsettled and the northern frontier open, sent the hostages home with rich gifts.

sentences.zh: 是時贤自负兵强，欲并兼西域，攻擊益甚。

translations.literal: At this time Xian prided himself on strong troops, wished to annex and merge the Western Regions, and attacks grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, confident in his army, aimed to conquer the entire Tarim and redoubled his campaigns.

sentences.zh: 諸國聞都護不出，而侍子皆還，大忧恐，乃與敦煌太守檄，愿留侍子以示莎車，言侍子见留，都護寻出，冀且息其兵。

translations.literal: The various states heard the Protector-General would not emerge and attendant sons all returned; greatly worried and fearful, then jointly with the Dunhuang governor issued proclamations, wishing to detain attendant sons to show Shache, saying attendant sons were being detained, Protector-General would soon emerge, hoping temporarily to halt his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that no Protector-General was coming and that hostages had been sent home, the kings panicked and petitioned Dunhuang to keep their sons as a signal to Yarkand that Han would soon appoint a Protector-General—anything to check Xian.

sentences.zh: 裴遵以状聞，天子許之。

translations.literal: Pei Zun reported the situation; the Son of Heaven granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Zun relayed the plea and the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，贤知都護不至，遂遗鄯善王安書，令絕通汉道。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, Xian knew the Protector-General would not arrive; thereupon sent King An of Shanshan a letter, ordering him to sever communication with Han roads.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, seeing no Protector-General, Xian ordered the king of Shanshan to cut the trade route to Han.

sentences.zh: 安不納而杀其使。

translations.literal: An did not accept and killed his envoy.
translations.idiomatic: An refused and executed Xian's messenger.

sentences.zh: 贤大怒，發兵攻鄯善。

translations.literal: Xian greatly angry, mobilized troops and attacked Shanshan.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged, Xian marched on Shanshan.

sentences.zh: 安迎战，兵败，亡入山中。

translations.literal: An met battle; army defeated; fled into the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: An gave battle, lost, and fled into the hills.

sentences.zh: 贤杀略千餘人而去。

translations.literal: Xian killed and plundered over one thousand persons and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Xian slaughtered and carried off more than a thousand people before withdrawing.

sentences.zh: 其冬，贤復攻杀龜兹王，遂兼其國。

translations.literal: That winter, Xian again attacked and killed the king of Qiuci, thereupon annexed its state.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he struck Kucha, slew its king, and annexed the realm.

sentences.zh: 鄯善、焉耆諸國侍子久留敦煌，愁思，皆亡歸。

translations.literal: Shanshan, Yanqi, and various states' attendant sons long detained at Dunhuang, sorrowful and longing, all fled home.
translations.idiomatic: The stranded hostages from Shanshan and Yanqi broke homeward from Dunhuang in despair.

sentences.zh: 鄯善王上書，愿復遣子入侍，更請都護。

translations.literal: The king of Shanshan submitted a memorial, wishing again to dispatch a son to attend court, again requesting a Protector-General.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Shanshan memorialized anew, offering hostages and begging for a Protector-General.

sentences.zh: 都護不出，诚迫于匈奴。

translations.literal: Protector-General does not emerge; truly pressed by the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: Without a Protector-General they had no choice but to yield to the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 天子報曰：「今使者大兵未能得出，如諸國力不从心，東西南北自在也。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven replied saying: “Now envoys and great troops are not yet able to emerge; if the various states' strength does not reach their hearts, east west south north are at liberty.”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered that Han could not yet dispatch armies; if the oasis kings lacked the strength to resist, they might align as circumstances required.

sentences.zh: 」於是鄯善、車師復附匈奴，而贤益横。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon Shanshan and Cheshi again attached to the Xiongnu, while Xian grew more domineering.
translations.idiomatic: Shanshan and Cheshi therefore submitted again to the Xiongnu while Xian grew bolder.

sentences.zh: 妫塞王自以國遠，遂杀贤使者，贤擊灭之，立其國贵人驷鞬為妫塞王。

translations.literal: The king of Guisai, because he thought his state distant, thereupon killed Xian's envoys; Xian struck and destroyed him, and established the state's noble Sijian as king of Guisai.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Guisai, confident in his remoteness, murdered Xian's envoys; Xian destroyed the kingdom and enthroned the noble Sijian.

sentences.zh: 贤又自立其子則罗為龜兹王。

translations.literal: Xian again established his own son Zeluo as king of Qiuci.
translations.idiomatic: Xian then installed his son Zeluo as king of Kucha.

sentences.zh: 贤以則罗年少，乃分龜兹為烏垒國，徙驷鞬為烏垒王，又更以贵人為妫塞王。

translations.literal: Xian because Zeluo was young, then divided Qiuci into the State of Wulei, moved Sijian to be king of Wulei, and again used another noble as king of Guisai.
translations.idiomatic: Finding Zeluo too young to rule, Xian carved Kucha into a new kingdom called Wulei, moved Sijian there as king, and appointed another noble over Guisai.

sentences.zh: 數歲，龜兹國人共杀則罗、驷鞬，而遣使匈奴，更請立王。

translations.literal: After several years, Qiuci state's people together killed Zeluo and Sijian, and dispatched envoys to the Xiongnu, again requesting establishment of a king.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years the people of Kucha slew Zeluo and Sijian and begged the Xiongnu to choose a new king.

sentences.zh: 匈奴立龜兹贵人身毒為龜兹王，龜兹由是屬匈奴。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu established Qiuci noble Shendu as king of Qiuci; Qiuci from this belonged to the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu enthroned the Kuchean noble Shendu, and Kucha henceforth answered to them.

sentences.zh: 贤以大宛貢税减少，自將諸國兵數萬人攻大宛，大宛王延留迎降，贤因將還國，徙拘彌王桥塞提為大宛王。

translations.literal: Xian because Dayuan's tribute taxes diminished, personally led various states' troops several tens of thousands to attack Dayuan; King Yanliu of Dayuan met and surrendered; Xian therefore led back to the state, moved Jumi king Qiaosaiti to be king of Dayuan.
translations.idiomatic: Angered by falling tribute from Ferghana, Xian led a coalition army west; Yanliu surrendered at once, so Xian marched home and transferred Jumi's king Qiaosaiti onto the Ferghana throne.

sentences.zh: 而康居數攻之，桥塞提在國歲餘，亡歸，贤復以為拘彌王，而遣延留還大宛，使貢獻如常。

translations.literal: But Kangju repeatedly attacked him; Qiaosaiti was in the state over a year, fled back; Xian again made him king of Jumi, and sent Yanliu back to Dayuan, causing tribute presentation as usual.
translations.idiomatic: Kangju raids drove Qiaosaiti out within a year; Xian restored him in Jumi, returned Yanliu to Ferghana, and resumed tribute.

sentences.zh: 贤又徙于窴王俞林為骊歸王，立其弟位侍為于窴王。

translations.literal: Xian again moved Yutian king Yulin to be king of Ligui, established his younger brother Weishi as king of Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: He demoted Khotan's Yulin to Ligui and enthroned Weishi in his place.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，贤疑諸國欲畔，召位侍及拘彌、姑墨、子合王，尽杀之，不復置王，但遣將镇守其國。

translations.literal: After over a year, Xian suspected the various states wished to rebel, summoned Weishi and kings of Jumi, Gumo, and Zihe, all killed them, no longer established kings, only dispatched generals to guard and hold their states.
translations.idiomatic: A year later, suspecting revolt, Xian summoned Weishi and the kings of Jumi, Gumo, and Zihe and executed them all, replacing royal rule with military governors.

sentences.zh: 位侍子戎亡降汉。

translations.literal: Weishi's son Rong fled and surrendered to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Weishi's son Rong escaped to Han.

sentences.zh: 封為守节侯。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Marquis Shoujie.
translations.idiomatic: The court enfeoffed him as Marquis Shoujie.

sentences.zh: 莎車將君得在于窴暴虐，百姓患之。

translations.literal: Suoche general Junde was in Yutian cruel and tyrannical; common people suffered from him.
translations.idiomatic: Junde, Yarkand's garrison commander in Khotan, tyrannized the people.

sentences.zh: 明帝永平三年，其大人都末出城，见野豕，欲射之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's Yongping third year, his great man Dumo exited the city, saw a wild pig, wished to shoot it.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping 3 of Emperor Ming the chief Dumo left the city, spotted a wild boar, and drew his bow.

sentences.zh: 豕乃言曰：「无射我，我乃為汝杀君得。

translations.literal: The pig then spoke saying: “Do not shoot me; I will for you kill Junde.”
translations.idiomatic: The boar spoke: “Spare me and I will rid you of Junde.”

sentences.zh: 」都末因此即與兄弟共杀君得。

translations.literal: ” Dumo from this immediately with brothers together killed Junde.
translations.idiomatic: Dumo and his brothers then slew Junde.

sentences.zh: 而大人休莫霸復與汉人韩融等杀都末兄弟，自立為于窴王，復與拘彌國人攻杀莎車將在皮山者，引兵歸。

translations.literal: But great man Xiumoba again with Han man Han Rong and others killed Dumo's brothers, established himself as king of Yutian, again with Jumi state people attacked and killed Suoche generals at Pishan, led troops back.
translations.idiomatic: The chief Xiumoba then murdered Dumo and his kin with Han Rong's help, crowned himself king of Khotan, joined Jumi troops to wipe out Yarkand's garrison at Pishan, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 於是贤遣其太子、國相，將諸國兵二萬人擊休莫霸，霸迎與战，莎車兵败走，杀萬餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon Xian dispatched his heir apparent and state minister, leading various states' troops twenty thousand to strike Xiumoba; Xiumoba met and battled; Suoche army was defeated and fled, killing over ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Xian sent his heir and chancellor with twenty thousand allies against Xiumoba, who met them in battle and routed Yarkand, taking more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 贤復發諸國數萬人，自將擊休莫霸，霸復破之，斩杀过半，贤脱身走歸國。

translations.literal: Xian again mobilized various states several tens of thousands, personally led to strike Xiumoba; Xiumoba again defeated them, beheading and killing over half; Xian escaped alone and fled back to his state.
translations.idiomatic: Xian raised another host and led it himself; Xiumoba shattered the army, slaughtering more than half before Xian fled home alone.

sentences.zh: 休莫霸進圍莎車，中流矢死，兵乃退。

translations.literal: Xiumoba advanced and besieged Suoche; mid-way struck by an arrow he died; troops then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiumoba pressed the siege of Yarkand but fell to an arrow; his army retreated.

sentences.zh: 于窴國相蘇榆勒等共立休莫霸兄子广德為王。

translations.literal: Yutian state ministers Suyule and others together established Xiumoba's elder brother's son Guangde as king.
translations.idiomatic: Khotan's ministers, led by Suyule, raised Xiumoba's nephew Guangde to the throne.

sentences.zh: 匈奴與龜兹諸國共攻莎車，不能下。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu together with Qiuci and various states jointly attacked Suoche; could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiongnu and Kucha-led coalition failed to storm Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 广德承莎車之敝，使弟辅國侯仁將兵攻贤。
