translations.literal: Guangde riding on Suoche's exhaustion, sent younger brother Marquis Fuguo Ren to lead troops to attack Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde exploited Yarkand's exhaustion and sent his brother Ren, Marquis Fuguo, against Xian.

sentences.zh: 贤連被兵革，乃遣使與广德和。

translations.literal: Xian repeatedly suffered weapons and armor; then dispatched envoys to make peace with Guangde.
translations.idiomatic: Hard-pressed by continuous war, Xian sued for peace.

sentences.zh: 先是广德父拘在莎車數歲，於是贤歸其父，而以女妻之，结為昆弟，广德引兵去。

translations.literal: Earlier Guangde's father had been detained at Suoche several years; thereupon Xian returned his father and gave his daughter as wife to him, bonded as sworn brothers; Guangde led troops away.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde's father had long been held at Yarkand; Xian now released him, married Guangde to his daughter, swore brotherhood, and Guangde withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，莎車相且运等患贤骄暴，密谋反城降于窴。

translations.literal: The next year, Suoche ministers Qieyun and others worried about Xian's arrogant violence, secretly plotted to turn the city and surrender to Yutian.
translations.idiomatic: The following year ministers such as Qieyun, weary of Xian's cruelty, plotted to open the gates to Khotan.

sentences.zh: 于窴王广德乃將諸國兵三萬人攻莎車。

translations.literal: Yutian king Guangde then led various states' troops thirty thousand to attack Suoche.
translations.idiomatic: Guangde then marched thirty thousand allied troops against Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 贤城守，使使谓广德曰：「我還汝父，與汝妇，汝來擊我，何為？

translations.literal: Xian defended the city, sent envoy to tell Guangde saying: “I returned your father and gave you my daughter as wife; you come to attack me—why?”
translations.idiomatic: From behind the walls Xian demanded of Guangde: “I freed your father and gave you my daughter—why attack me now?”

sentences.zh: 」广德曰：「王，我妇父也，久不相见，愿各从两人会城外结盟。

translations.literal: ” Guangde said: “King, you are my wife's father; long we have not seen each other; wish each to follow two persons and meet outside the city to covenant alliance.”
translations.idiomatic: Guangde answered: “You are my wife's father; we have been apart too long—let each of us bring two companions and swear an oath beyond the walls.”

sentences.zh: 」贤以问且运，且运曰：「广德女婿，至亲，宜出见之。

translations.literal: ” Xian asked Qieyun; Qieyun said: “Guangde is son-in-law; utmost kin—it is fitting to go out and see him.”
translations.idiomatic: Xian consulted Qieyun, who urged him to go—Guangde was family.

sentences.zh: 」贤乃轻出，广德遂执贤。

translations.literal: ” Xian then lightly went out; Guangde thereupon seized Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Trusting the advice, Xian rode out lightly and Guangde seized him.

sentences.zh: 而且运等因内于窴兵，虜贤妻子而并其國。

translations.literal: Moreover Qieyun and others then admitted Yutian troops inside, captured Xian's wife and children and annexed his state.
translations.idiomatic: Qieyun admitted Khotanese troops, seized Xian's family, and annexed Yarkand.

sentences.zh: 锁贤將歸，歲餘杀之。

translations.literal: They shackled Xian and led him back; after over a year killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They marched Xian away in chains and executed him after a year.

sentences.zh: 匈奴聞广德灭莎車，遣五將發焉耆、尉黎、龜兹十五國兵三萬餘人圍于窴，广德乞降，以其太子為質，约歲给罽絮。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu heard Guangde extinguished Suoche, dispatched five generals mobilizing Yanqi, Weili, Qiuci fifteen states' troops over thirty thousand to besiege Yutian; Guangde begged to surrender, took his heir apparent as hostage, agreed yearly to supply felts and floss.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Guangde had destroyed Yarkand, the Xiongnu sent five generals with thirty thousand men from fifteen states to besiege Khotan; Guangde capitulated, surrendered his heir, and promised annual tribute of woolens.

sentences.zh: 冬，匈奴復遣兵將贤質子不居徵立為莎車王，广德又攻杀之，更立其弟齐黎為莎車王，章帝元和三年也。

translations.literal: Winter, the Xiongnu again dispatched troops installing Xian's hostage son Bujuzheng as king of Suoche; Guangde again attacked and killed him, again established his younger brother Qili as king of Suoche—it was Emperor Zhang's Yuanhe third year.
translations.idiomatic: That winter the Xiongnu placed Xian's hostage Bujuzheng on the Yarkand throne; Guangde stormed the city, killed him, and enthroned Bujuzheng's brother Qili—this was Yuanhe 3 of Emperor Zhang.

sentences.zh: 時，長史班超發諸國兵擊莎車，大破之，由是遂降汉。

translations.literal: At that time, Chief Clerk Ban Chao mobilized various states' troops to strike Suoche, greatly defeated them; from this then surrendered to Han.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Clerk Ban Chao then rallied the allies, shattered Yarkand, and brought it back under Han.

sentences.zh: 事已惧《班超傳》。

translations.literal: The affairs afterward are detailed in the Biography of Ban Chao.
translations.idiomatic: The rest of the story appears in Ban Chao's biography.

sentences.zh: 莎車東北至疏勒。

translations.literal: Suoche northeast reaches Shule.
translations.idiomatic: Yarkand lies northeast of Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 疏勒國

translations.literal: The State of Shule.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Shule (Kashgar).

sentences.zh: 疏勒國，去長史所居五千里，去洛陽萬三百里。

translations.literal: The State of Shule is five thousand li from the Chief Clerk's residence, ten thousand three hundred li from Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Kashgar stood 5,000 li from the chief clerk's headquarters and 10,300 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 領户二萬一千，胜兵三萬餘人。

translations.literal: It leads households twenty-one thousand, victorious soldiers over thirty thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: It numbered 21,000 households and more than 30,000 troops under arms.

sentences.zh: 明帝永平十六年，龜兹王建攻杀疏勒王成，自以龜兹左侯兜题為疏勒王。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's Yongping sixteenth year, Qiuci king Jian attacked and killed Shule king Cheng, himself appointed Qiuci Left Marquis Douti as Shule king.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongping 16 Jian of Kucha killed Kashgar's king Cheng and installed his officer Douti as puppet ruler.

sentences.zh: 冬，汉遣軍司馬班超劫缚兜题，而立成之兄子忠為疏勒王。

translations.literal: Winter, Han dispatched Army Major Ban Chao to seize and bind Douti, and established Cheng's elder brother's son Zhong as king of Shule.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Army Major Ban Chao seized Douti and enthroned Zhong, a nephew of the murdered king Cheng.

sentences.zh: 忠後反畔，超擊斩之。

translations.literal: Zhong afterward rebelled and turned away; Chao struck and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhong later rebelled, Ban Chao executed him.

sentences.zh: 事已具《超傳》。

translations.literal: The affair afterward is fully set out in the Biography of Chao.
translations.idiomatic: The full account appears in Ban Chao's biography.

sentences.zh: 安帝元初中，疏勒王安國以舅臣磐有罪，徙于月氏。

translations.literal: In Emperor An's Yuanchu era, King Anguo of Shule, because his maternal uncle Chenpan was guilty, was exiled to the Yuezhi.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yuanchu years, King Anguo of Kashgar exiled his uncle Chenpan to the Yuezhi for a crime.

sentences.zh: 月氏王亲爱之。

translations.literal: The Yuezhi king was intimate and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: The Kushan king favored Chenpan.

sentences.zh: 後安國死，无子，母持國政，與國人共立臣磐同产弟子遗腹為疏勒王。

translations.literal: Later Anguo died, without son; the mother held state power; together with the state's people they established Chenpan's uterine younger brother's son Yifu as king of Shule.
translations.idiomatic: When Anguo died without an heir, the queen mother ruled and the nobles enthroned Yifu, Chenpan's nephew by the same mother.

sentences.zh: 臣磐聞之，請月氏王曰：「安國无子，种人微弱，若立母氏，我乃遗腹叔父也，我当為王。

translations.literal: Chenpan heard it, begged the Yuezhi king saying: “Anguo has no son; the royal seed is feeble; if the mother's clan is set up, I am Yifu's paternal uncle—I ought to be king.”
translations.idiomatic: Chenpan petitioned the Kushan king: “Anguo left no son; the royal line is weak. If a queen's faction rules, I am Yifu's uncle and the rightful king.”

sentences.zh: 」月氏乃遣兵送還疏勒。

translations.literal: ” The Yuezhi then dispatched troops to escort him back to Shule.
translations.idiomatic: The Kushans sent troops to restore Chenpan to Kashgar.

sentences.zh: 國人素敬爱臣磐，又畏惮月氏，即共夺遗腹印绶，迎臣磐立為王，更以遗腹為磐稿城侯。

translations.literal: The state's people long revered and loved Chenpan, and again feared the Yuezhi; immediately together they seized Yifu's seal-cord, welcomed Chenpan and established him as king, and changed Yifu to be Chenpan's Gaocheng marquis.
translations.idiomatic: The nobles, who honored Chenpan and feared the Kushans, stripped Yifu of his seal, enthroned Chenpan, and reduced Yifu to Marquis of Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 後莎車連畔于窴，屬疏勒，疏勒以强，故得與龜兹、于窴為敌國焉。

translations.literal: Later Suoche repeatedly turned against Yutian, attached to Shule; Shule by strength therefore was able with Qiuci and Yutian to be rival states.
translations.idiomatic: When Yarkand broke with Khotan and entered Kashgar's orbit, Kashgar grew strong enough to stand as a third power against Kucha and Khotan.

sentences.zh: 東北經尉头、温宿、姑墨、龜兹至焉耆。

translations.literal: Northeast passes Weitou, Wensu, Gumo, Qiuci to Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: Northeastward the road runs through Weitou, Aksu, Gumo, and Kucha to Karashahr.

sentences.zh: 焉耆國

translations.literal: The State of Yanqi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Yanqi (Karashahr).

sentences.zh: 焉耆國王居南河城，北去長史所居八百里，東去洛陽八千二百里。

translations.literal: The king of the State of Yanqi dwells at Nanhe city; north from the Chief Clerk's residence eight hundred li; east from Luoyang eight thousand two hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: The king ruled from Nanhe—800 li north of the chief clerk's camp and 8,200 li west of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 户萬五千，口五萬二千，胜兵二萬餘人。

translations.literal: Households fifteen thousand, mouths fifty-two thousand, victorious soldiers over twenty thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: It counted 15,000 households, 52,000 people, and more than 20,000 soldiers.

sentences.zh: 其國四面有大山，與龜兹相連，道險厄，易守。

translations.literal: Its state on four sides has great mountains; it connects with Qiuci; roads are perilous and narrow; easy to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Ringed by mountains and linked by dangerous roads to Kucha, it was easy to defend.

sentences.zh: 有海水曲入四山之内，周匝其城三十餘里。

translations.literal: There is sea water bending inward within the four mountains; it encircles its city over thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: A lake curls among the peaks and belts the capital for more than thirty li.

sentences.zh: 永平末，焉耆與龜兹共攻沒都護陳睦、副校尉郭恂，杀吏士二千餘人。

translations.literal: At the end of Yongping, Yanqi together with Qiuci jointly attacked and destroyed Protector-General Chen Mu and Vice Colonel Guo Xun, killing over two thousand officials and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yongping, Yanqi and Kucha jointly destroyed Protector-General Chen Mu and Vice Colonel Guo Xun and slew over two thousand Han troops.

sentences.zh: 至永元六年，都護班超發諸國兵讨焉耆、危须、尉黎、山國，遂斩焉耆、尉黎二王首，傳送京師，縣蛮夷邸。

translations.literal: By Yongyuan sixth year, Protector-General Ban Chao mobilized various states' troops to punish Yanqi, Weixu, Weili, Shanguo; thereupon beheaded Yanqi and Weili two kings' heads, transmitted them to the capital, hung them at the barbarian hostel.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongyuan 6 Ban Chao led an allied army against Yanqi, Weixu, Korla, and the mountain states; he sent the heads of the kings of Yanqi and Korla to Luoyang for display.

sentences.zh: 超乃立焉耆左候元孟為王，尉黎、危须、山國皆更立其王。

translations.literal: Chao then established Yanqi Left Marquis Yuan Meng as king; Weili, Weixu, Shanguo all replaced their kings.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Chao enthroned Yuan Meng in Yanqi and installed new rulers in Korla, Weixu, and the mountain chiefdoms.

sentences.zh: 至安帝時，西域背畔。

translations.literal: By Emperor An's time, the Western Regions rebelled and turned away.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor An the Tarim states rebelled.

sentences.zh: 延光中，超子勇為西域長史，復讨定諸國。

translations.literal: In Yanguang, Chao's son Yong was Chief Clerk of the Western Regions; again attacked and pacified the various states.
translations.idiomatic: During Yanguang, Ban Yong as chief clerk reconquered the oases.

sentences.zh: 元孟與尉黎、危须不降。

translations.literal: Yuan Meng together with Weili and Weixu did not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Meng held Korla and Weixu against Han.

sentences.zh: 永建二年，勇與敦煌太守張朗擊破之，元孟乃遣子詣阙貢獻。

translations.literal: In Yongjian second year, Yong together with Dunhuang governor Zhang Lang struck and defeated them; Yuan Meng then dispatched his son to the palace to offer tribute.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjian 2 Ban Yong and Zhang Lang of Dunhuang crushed the coalition; Yuan Meng then sent his son to court with tribute.

sentences.zh: 蒲類國

translations.literal: The State of Pulei.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Pulei (Barkol).

sentences.zh: 蒲類國，居天山西疏榆谷，東南去長史所居千二百九十里，去洛陽萬四百九十里。

translations.literal: The State of Pulei dwells at Shuyu valley west of the Tianshan; southeast from the Chief Clerk's residence one thousand two hundred ninety li; from Luoyang ten thousand four hundred ninety li.
translations.idiomatic: Pulei occupied Shuyu west of the Tianshan—1,290 li southeast of the chief clerk's headquarters and 10,490 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 户八百餘，口二千餘，胜兵七百餘人。

translations.literal: Households over eight hundred, mouths over two thousand, victorious soldiers over seven hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: It mustered some 800 households, 2,000 people, and 700 troops.

sentences.zh: 庐帐而居，逐水草，颇知田作。

translations.literal: They dwell in felt tents, follow water and grass, somewhat know field cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in yurts, followed pasture, and practiced limited farming.

sentences.zh: 有牛、馬、骆驼、羊畜。

translations.literal: They have cattle, horses, camels, sheep livestock.
translations.idiomatic: They kept cattle, horses, camels, and sheep.

sentences.zh: 能作弓矢。

translations.literal: They can make bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: They forged bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 國出好馬。

translations.literal: The state produces fine horses.
translations.idiomatic: The land bred excellent horses.

sentences.zh: 蒲類本大國也，前西域屬匈奴，而其王得罪单于，单于怒，徙蒲類人六千餘口，内之匈奴右部阿恶地，因号曰阿恶國。

translations.literal: Pulei was originally a great state; formerly the Western Regions belonged to the Xiongnu, but its king offended the Chanyu; the Chanyu angry, moved over six thousand mouths of Pulei people, settled them in the Xiongnu right wing Awu territory; therefore titled Awu State.
translations.idiomatic: Pulei had once been large; when its king offended the Chanyu, the court resettled six thousand people in Awu on the right wing of the Xiongnu confederation, hence the name Awu.

sentences.zh: 南去車師後部馬行九十餘日。

translations.literal: South from Rear Cheshi by horse over ninety days.
translations.idiomatic: From Awu it was ninety days' ride south to Rear Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 人口贫羸，逃亡山谷间，故留為國云。

translations.literal: Population poor and emaciated, fled hiding in mountain valleys; therefore remained as a state it is said.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant poor hid in the hills—this is how the petty polity survived.

sentences.zh: 移支國

translations.literal: The State of Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 移支國，居蒲類地。

translations.literal: The State of Yizhi dwells in Pulei territory.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi occupied the Barkol region.

sentences.zh: 户千餘，口三千餘，胜兵千餘人。

translations.literal: Households over one thousand, mouths over three thousand, victorious soldiers over one thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: It counted upward of 1,000 households, 3,000 people, and 1,000 warriors.

sentences.zh: 其人勇猛敢战，以寇鈔為事。

translations.literal: Its people are fierce brave and dare fight; they take raiding and plunder as occupation.
translations.idiomatic: They were fierce raiders who lived by plunder.

sentences.zh: 皆被發，随畜逐水草，不知田作。

translations.literal: All wear hair loose, follow livestock pursuing water and grass; do not know field cultivation.
translations.idiomatic: They wore their hair loose, followed the herds, and did not farm.

sentences.zh: 所出皆與蒲類同。

translations.literal: What they produce is all the same as Pulei.
translations.idiomatic: Their produce matched Pulei's.

sentences.zh: 東且彌國

translations.literal: The State of Eastern Juemi.
translations.idiomatic: The kingdom of Eastern Juemi.

sentences.zh: 東且彌國，東去長史所居八百里，去洛陽九千二百五十里。

translations.literal: The State of Eastern Juemi, east from the Chief Clerk's residence eight hundred li; from Luoyang nine thousand two hundred fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Juemi lay 800 li east of the chief clerk's seat and 9,250 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 户三千餘，口五千餘，胜兵二千餘人。

translations.literal: Households over three thousand, mouths over five thousand, victorious soldiers over two thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: It had over 3,000 households, 5,000 people, and more than 2,000 soldiers.

sentences.zh: 庐帐居，逐水草，颇田作。

translations.literal: They dwell in felt tents, follow water and grass, somewhat field cultivate.
translations.idiomatic: They lived in yurts, followed pasture, and farmed a little.

sentences.zh: 其所出有亦與蒲類同。

translations.literal: What they produce also is the same as Pulei.
translations.idiomatic: Their exports were the same as Pulei's.

sentences.zh: 所居无常。

translations.literal: Where they dwell is not constant.
translations.idiomatic: They had no fixed settlements.

sentences.zh: 車師前王居交河城。

translations.literal: Front Cheshi king dwells at Jiaohe city.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Front Cheshi ruled from Jiaohe.

sentences.zh: 河水分流绕城，故号交河。

translations.literal: River waters divide flow surround the city; therefore titled Intersecting Rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Two rivers bracket the town—hence “Jiaohe,” the Confluence.

sentences.zh: 去長史所居柳中八十里，東去洛陽九千一百二十里。

translations.literal: From the Chief Clerk's residence Liuzhong eighty li; east from Luoyang nine thousand one hundred twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: It was 80 li from Liuzhong and 9,120 li west of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 領户千五百餘，口四千餘，胜兵二千人。

translations.literal: It leads households over one thousand five hundred, mouths over four thousand, victorious soldiers two thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: It numbered some 1,500 households, 4,000 people, and 2,000 troops.

sentences.zh: 後王居务涂谷，去長史所居五百里，去洛陽九千六百二十里。

translations.literal: The rear king dwells at Wutugu valley; from the Chief Clerk's residence five hundred li; from Luoyang nine thousand six hundred twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: The rear king held court at Wutugu—500 li from the chief clerk's headquarters and 9,620 li from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 領户四千餘，口萬五千餘，胜兵三千餘人。

translations.literal: It leads households over four thousand, mouths over fifteen thousand, victorious soldiers over three thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: It mustered over 4,000 households, 15,000 people, and more than 3,000 soldiers.

sentences.zh: 前後部及東且彌、卑陆、蒲類、移支，是為車師六國，北與匈奴接，前部西通焉耆北道，後部西通烏孙。

translations.literal: Front and rear divisions together with Eastern Juemi, Beilu, Pulei, Yizhi—these are Cheshi six states; north they connect with the Xiongnu; front division west connects Yanqi northern route; rear division west connects Wusun.
translations.idiomatic: Front and Rear Cheshi plus Eastern Juemi, Beilu, Pulei, and Yizhi formed the six Cheshi polities—bordering the Xiongnu on the north, Front Cheshi opening the northern road to Yanqi, Rear Cheshi linking west to Wusun.

sentences.zh: 建武二十一年，與鄯善、焉耆遣子入侍，光武遣還之，乃附屬匈奴。

translations.literal: In Jianwu twenty-first year, together with Shanshan and Yanqi dispatched sons to attend court; Guangwu sent them back; thereupon attached to the Xiongnu.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu 21 Cheshi joined Shanshan and Yanqi in sending hostages; Guangwu returned them, and Cheshi submitted to the Xiongnu.

sentences.zh: 明帝永平十六年，汉取伊吾盧，通西域，車師始復内屬。

translations.literal: In Emperor Ming's Yongping sixteenth year, Han took Yiwulu, connected the Western Regions; Cheshi then first again internally depended.
translations.idiomatic: When Han seized Yiwu in Yongping 16 and reopened the western roads, Cheshi renewed its ties to the interior.

sentences.zh: 匈奴遣兵擊之，復降北虜。

translations.literal: The Xiongnu dispatched troops to strike them; again surrendered to the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Xiongnu attacks forced them to yield again.

sentences.zh: 和帝永元二年，大將軍竇憲破北匈奴，車師震慑，前後王各遣子奉貢入侍，并赐印绶金帛。

translations.literal: In Emperor He's Yongyuan second year, Grand General Dou Xian broke the northern Xiongnu; Cheshi trembled in awe; front and rear kings each dispatched sons presenting tribute to attend court; together were bestowed seal-cords, gold, and silks.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Xian crushed the northern Xiongnu in Yongyuan 2, both Cheshi kings sent hostages and received seals and gifts.

sentences.zh: 八年，戊己校尉索頵欲废後部王涿鞮，立破虜侯细致。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Gengji Colonel Suo Xun wished to depose rear king Zhuodi, establish Marquis Polu Xizhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the era Colonel Suo Xun tried to replace Rear King Zhuodi with Xizhi, Marquis Polu.

sentences.zh: 涿鞮忿前王尉卑大卖己，因反擊尉卑大，获其妻子。

translations.literal: Zhuodi resented former king Weibeida for betraying him; therefore turned and attacked Weibeida, captured his wife and children.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuodi, furious that the former king Weibeida had betrayed him, struck Front Cheshi, taking his family captive.

sentences.zh: 明年，汉遣將兵長史王林，發凉州六郡兵及羌胡二萬餘人，以讨涿鞮，获首虜千餘人。

translations.literal: The next year, Han dispatched Colonel-in-Chief Secretary Wang Lin, mobilized Liangzhou six commanderies' troops and Qiang and Hu over twenty thousand persons, to punish Zhuodi, captured heads and captives over one thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: The following year Wang Lin led twenty thousand troops from Liangzhou against Zhuodi and took more than a thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 涿鞮入北匈奴，汉軍追擊，斩之，立涿鞮弟农奇為王。

translations.literal: Zhuodi entered northern Xiongnu; Han army pursued and struck, beheaded him, established Zhuodi's younger brother Nongqi as king.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuodi fled to the northern Xiongnu; Han troops ran him down and killed him, enthroning his brother Nongqi.

sentences.zh: 至永寧元年，後王軍就及母沙麻反畔，杀後部司馬及敦煌行事。

translations.literal: By Yongning first year, rear king Junjiu and mother Shama rebelled and turned away, killed rear colonel and Dunhuang administrator.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongning 1 Rear King Junjiu and his mother Shama rebelled, murdering the colonel of Rear Cheshi and the Dunhuang deputy.

sentences.zh: 至安帝延光四年，長史班勇擊軍就，大破，斩之。

translations.literal: By Emperor An's Yanguang fourth year, Chief Clerk Ban Yong struck Junjiu, greatly defeated him, beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanguang 4 of Emperor An, Ban Yong shattered Junjiu's army and executed him.

sentences.zh: 顺帝永建元年，勇率後王农奇子加特奴及八滑等，發精兵擊北虜呼衍王，破之。

translations.literal: In Emperor Shun's Yongjian first year, Yong led rear king Nongqi's sons Jiatenu and Bahua and others, mobilized crack troops to strike northern barbarians' King Huyan, defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongjian 1 Ban Yong led Jiatenu, Bahua, and picked troops against the Xiongnu King Huyan and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 勇於是上立加特奴為後王，八滑為後部亲汉侯。

translations.literal: Yong thereupon presented upward establishing Jiatenu as rear king, Bahua as Rear Division Pro-Han Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: Ban Yong then invested Jiatenu as rear king and Bahua as marquis of the Pro-Han rear division.

sentences.zh: 陽嘉三年夏，車師後部司馬率加特奴等千五百人，掩擊北匈奴于阊吾陆谷，坏其庐落，斩數百级，获单于母、季母及妇女數百人，牛、羊十餘萬头，車千餘两，兵器什物甚眾。

translations.literal: Yangjia third year summer, Rear Cheshi major led Jiatenu and others fifteen hundred persons, surprise-attacked northern Xiongnu at Changwulu valley, destroyed their felt halls, beheaded several hundred ranks, captured Chanyu's mother, aunt, and women several hundred persons, cattle and sheep over one hundred thousand head, carts over one thousand carriages, weapons and miscellaneous goods very many.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the Rear Cheshi major led fifteen hundred men under Jiatenu in a raid on Huyan's camp at Changwulu, wrecked the nomad settlements, killed hundreds, captured the Chanyu's mother and other women, drove off a hundred thousand head of stock and a thousand carts, and seized heaps of arms.

sentences.zh: 四年春，北匈奴呼衍王率兵侵後部，帝以車師六國接近北虜，為西域蔽扞，乃令敦煌太守發諸國兵，及玉門關候、伊吾司馬，合六千三百騎救之，掩擊北虜于勒山，汉軍不利。

translations.literal: Fourth year spring, northern Xiongnu King Huyan led troops invading rear division; the emperor because Cheshi six states neared northern barbarians, were western regions screen and shield, therefore ordered Dunhuang governor to mobilize various states' troops, together with Yumen Pass warden, Yiwu major, altogether six thousand three hundred horse to rescue them, surprise-attacked northern barbarians at Mount Le; Han army was unlucky.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring Huyan struck Rear Cheshi; treating the six Cheshi states as Han's shield on the steppe, the court ordered Dunhuang to rally 6,300 cavalry from the oases, Yumen, and Yiwu for a spoiling attack at Mount Le—the Han force fared badly.

sentences.zh: 秋，呼衍王復將二千人攻後部，破之。

translations.literal: Autumn, King Huyan again led two thousand men attacking rear division, defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Huyan returned with two thousand riders and crushed Rear Cheshi.

sentences.zh: 桓帝元嘉元年，呼衍王將三千餘騎寇伊吾，伊吾司馬毛恺遣吏兵五百人于蒲類海東與呼衍王战，悉為所沒，呼衍王遂攻伊吾屯城。

translations.literal: Emperor Huan's Yuanjia first year, King Huyan led over three thousand riders raiding Yiwu; Yiwu major Mao Kai dispatched clerks and soldiers five hundred persons east of Barkol Sea to battle King Huyan; all were destroyed by them; King Huyan then attacked Yiwu garrison city.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia 1 of Emperor Huan, Huyan swept down on Yiwu with three thousand riders; Major Mao Kai lost five hundred men east of Barkol Lake—every man killed—and Huyan pressed the Han fort.

sentences.zh: 夏，遣敦煌太守司馬达將敦煌、酒泉，張掖屬國吏士四千餘人救之，出塞至蒲類海，呼衍王聞而引去，汉軍无功而還。

translations.literal: Summer, dispatched Dunhuang governor Sima Da leading Dunhuang, Jiuquan, Zhangye dependent state officials and soldiers over four thousand persons to rescue them; exited the barrier to Barkol Sea; King Huyan heard and drew away; Han army without achievement returned.
translations.idiomatic: That summer Sima Da led four thousand men from Dunhuang, Jiuquan, and Zhangye beyond the wall to Barkol Sea; Huyan withdrew and the Han column returned empty-handed.

sentences.zh: 论曰：西域風土之載，前古未聞也。

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Records of the Western Regions' customs and soil—in former antiquity were unheard.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: Accounts of the Western Regions had no precedent in earlier ages.

sentences.zh: 汉世張骞懷致遠之略，班超奋封侯之志，终能立功西遐，羈服外域。

translations.literal: In Han times Zhang Qian cherished strategies for reaching the distant; Ban Chao roused ambitions for noble rank; ultimately could establish merit in the remote west and tie and submit outer regions.
translations.idiomatic: In Han, Zhang Qian conceived the outreach to the west and Ban Chao strove for noble honors; both earned merit on the frontier and brought distant realms to heel.

sentences.zh: 自兵威之所肃服，財赂之所懷诱，莫不獻方奇，納爱質，露顶肘行，東向而朝天子。

translations.literal: From where military awe subdued them and wealth bribes enticed them—none failed to present regional marvels, send cherished hostages, bare crown and crawl on elbows, face east and court the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Whether coerced by arms or coaxed with treasure, every oasis sent rarities and hostages, crawling eastward in submission to bow before the throne.

sentences.zh: 故設戊己之官，分任其事；

translations.literal: Therefore established Gengji officials, dividing their duties;
translations.idiomatic: Hence Han posted Gengji colonels to divide frontier duties;

sentences.zh: 建都護之帥，总領其权。

translations.literal: Established Protector-General commanders, gathering overall their authority.
translations.idiomatic: and installed Protectors-General to hold supreme western authority.

sentences.zh: 先驯則赏籯金以赐龜绶，後服則系头颡而衅北阙。

translations.literal: Those who submitted early then were rewarded chest gold and granted tortoise cords; those who yielded later had heads bound at forehead and blood smeared at the northern gate tower.
translations.idiomatic: Early allies received gold and tortoise seals; late rebels were bound for execution beneath the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 立屯田于膏腴之野，列邮置于要害之路。

translations.literal: Established military colonies on fertile fat plains; arrayed post stations on crucial roads.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison farms covered the fertile valleys and courier relays guarded every choke point.

sentences.zh: 驰命走驿，不絕于時月；

translations.literal: Galloping orders running relays did not cease through seasons and months;
translations.idiomatic: Dispatch riders thundered along the posts without pause;

sentences.zh: 商胡贩客，日款于塞下。

translations.literal: Merchant Hu peddlers daily approached beneath the passes.
translations.idiomatic: while Sogdian traders crowded the frontier gates each day.

sentences.zh: 其後甘英乃抵條支而历安息，臨西海以望大秦，拒玉門、陽關者四萬餘里，靡不周尽焉。

translations.literal: Afterward Gan Ying then reached Tiaozhi and passed Anxi, faced the Western Sea gazing at Daqin—forty thousand li removed from Yumen and Yang Pass—none was not exhaustively thorough.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gan Ying traveled from Mesopotamia through Parthia to the Mediterranean rim—more than forty thousand li beyond the Jade and Yang Passes—and brought back nearly everything worth knowing.

sentences.zh: 若其境俗性智之优薄，产載物類之区品，川河領障之基源，气节凉暑之通隔，梯山栈谷、绳行沙度之道，身热首痛、風灾鬼難之域，莫不備写情形，审求根实。

translations.literal: As for their borders' customs and nature intelligence superior or thin, produce carriage creature kinds by grade, rivers ranges barrier origins, qi seasons cool heat connections and blocks, ladder mountains plank valleys rope-crossing sand routes, body fever head pain wind calamity ghost hardship domains—none failed completely to write circumstances, carefully seeking root truth.
translations.idiomatic: Customs and temperaments, exports and beasts, watersheds and climates, cliff roads and desert tracks, fevers and haunted wastes—the annals record each with care.

sentences.zh: 至于佛道神化，兴自身毒，而二汉方志，莫有称焉。

translations.literal: As for Buddha way divine transformation, arose from Shendu—yet Former and Later Han gazetteers none praised it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Buddhism, born in India, goes unmentioned in the Han regional histories.

sentences.zh: 張骞但著地多暑湿，乘象而战，班勇虽列其奉浮图，不杀伐，而精文善法、导达之功，靡所傳述。

translations.literal: Zhang Qian only noted the land was mostly hot damp, rode elephants to fight; Ban Yong although listed their revering stupas, not killing—yet refined texts good law, guiding merits, nowhere transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Qian spoke only of elephants and monsoon heat; Ban Yong noted stupas and ahimsa—but neither conveyed doctrine or translation.

sentences.zh: 餘聞之後说也，其國則殷乎中土，玉烛和气。

translations.literal: I have heard latter explanations: their land then flourishes like central soil, jade candle harmonious qi.
translations.idiomatic: Later tradition paints India as prosperous as China itself—temperate and blessed.

sentences.zh: 灵圣之所降集，贤懿之所挺生，神迹诡怪，則理絕人区，感验明显，則事出天外。

translations.literal: Where numinous sages descend gather, worthy virtuous rise born—divine traces bizarre strange then principle cuts off human realm; sensations verification manifest clear then affairs emerge beyond heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits and sages walk there; marvels exceed mortal reason when visions prove true they seem to fall from beyond the sky.

sentences.zh: 而骞、超无聞者，岂其道閉往运，數开叔叶乎？

translations.literal: Yet Qian and Chao heard nothing of it—could it be the Way was blocked in former destiny, fate opened in declining leaf-times?
translations.idiomatic: Why did Zhang Qian and Ban Chao miss it—because the teaching waited for a later age?

sentences.zh: 不然，何诬異之甚也！

translations.literal: If not so, why exaggerate strangeness so greatly!
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise later lore wildly overstates the exotic.

sentences.zh: 汉自楚英始盛斋戒之祀，桓帝又修华盖之饰。

translations.literal: Han from Chu Ying began flourishing fasting purity sacrifices; Emperor Huan again cultivated canopy adornments.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ying of Chu opened Han to Buddhist-style abstinence; Emperor Huan decked the palace for ritual.

sentences.zh: 將微义未譯，而但神明之邪？

translations.literal: Could it be subtle meaning not yet translated, therefore only spirit-divinity?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps because sutras had not yet been translated, converts worshipped only vague spirits?

sentences.zh: 詳其清心释累之训，空有兼遣之宗，道書之流也。

translations.literal: Examine its teaching pure heart shed burdens, emptiness-being jointly dispatched school—it flows with Daoist writings.
translations.idiomatic: Its counsel on purity and release from karma belongs with Daoist discourse on emptying both extremes.

sentences.zh: 且好仁恶杀，蠲敝崇善，所以贤达君子多爱其法焉。

translations.literal: Moreover cherishing benevolence hating killing, remitting ruin esteeming good—therefore worthy enlightened gentlemen mostly loved its law.
translations.idiomatic: Its mercy toward life won many thoughtful patrons.

sentences.zh: 然好大不經，奇谲无已，虽邹衍谈天之辩，庄周蜗角之论，尚未足以概其萬一。

translations.literal: Yet loving greatness not canonical, marvelous deceit without end—although Zou Yan's heaven discourse debate, Zhuang Zhou's snail-horn theory, still not sufficient to encompass its one ten-thousandth.
translations.idiomatic: Yet its cosmic tales outrun even Zou Yan's cosmology or Zhuangzi's parables.

sentences.zh: 又精灵起灭，因報相寻。

translations.literal: Again spirit essences rise extinguish; causes retribution chase each other.
translations.idiomatic: Spirits wax and wane; karma follows deed after deed.

sentences.zh: 若晓而昧者，故通人多惑焉。

translations.literal: Like knowing yet dark—therefore thorough scholars mostly were perplexed.
translations.idiomatic: Doctrine seems clear yet slips away—even scholars grew doubtful.

sentences.zh: 盖导俗无方，适物異会，取諸同歸，措夫疑说，則大道通矣。

translations.literal: For guiding customs without fixed method, suiting things divergent meetings, taking from shared return, placing doubtful theories—then the Great Way opens.
translations.idiomatic: Because customs vary, wise teachers meet each audience halfway—harmonize divergent glosses and the great truth opens.

sentences.zh: 赞曰：逷矣西胡，天之外区。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Far indeed western Hu—Heaven's outer regions.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Far dwell the western barbarians beyond Heaven's rim.

sentences.zh: 土物琛丽，人性淫虚。

translations.literal: Soil things treasure splendid; human nature excessive hollow.
translations.idiomatic: Their lands yield splendid treasures; their temperaments run to extravagance and guile.

sentences.zh: 不率华礼，莫有典書。

translations.literal: They do not follow Hua ritual; none have canonical writings.
translations.idiomatic: They keep no Chinese rites nor classical canon.

sentences.zh: 若微神道，何恤何拘！

translations.literal: If without divine Way—what pity what restraint!
translations.idiomatic: Without transcendent teaching to steady them, how could they be ruled or pitied?
